2026-01-01.headline: Per-rule ASR exclusions and privileged-account assessments sharpen Defender administration guidance
2026-01-01.overview: This was a documentation-led period with several operationally useful updates. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint guidance now documents per-rule ASR exclusions through Group Policy, PowerShell, and Intune. Defender for Identity release notes add assessments for service accounts in privileged groups and accounts in built-in Operator Groups, including direct, indirect, and nested membership. Endpoint procedures also clarify EDR testing, the TCP port 80 server prerequisite, the role required to undo contain-user actions, and the command-line process for restoring quarantined files.
2026-01-01.adminImpact: Review per-rule ASR exception workflows and use the platform-specific EDR test procedure. Identity administrators can use the new assessments to investigate elevated or unnecessary access. Operators who need to undo contain-user actions require Global Administrator membership in Microsoft Entra permissions, while server EDR tests require TCP port 80 to be listening. No deadline or broad rollout action is stated.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity adds privileged-access assessments
keyChanges.detail: The January release notes add assessments for service accounts in privileged groups and accounts in built-in Operator Groups, covering direct, indirect, and nested membership. Administrators can use them to identify elevated or unnecessary access.

keyChanges.title: ASR guidance documents exclusions for individual rules
keyChanges.detail: The enablement guidance now states that Group Policy, PowerShell, and Intune can configure exclusions for specific attack surface reduction rules, supporting more targeted exceptions than applying them across all rules.

keyChanges.title: EDR testing now separates client and server procedures
keyChanges.detail: Windows client instructions use PowerShell to create and rename an EICAR test file. Windows server instructions retain the download-and-run test and add a TCP port 80 prerequisite with a connectivity check; verify the port before testing a server.

keyChanges.title: Undoing contain-user actions requires Global Administrator
keyChanges.detail: The response-actions guidance now states that undoing contain-user actions requires membership in the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra permissions, alongside least-privilege guidance. Operators without that role cannot perform the operation.

keyChanges.title: MpCmdRun steps clarify quarantined-file restoration
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Defender Antivirus guidance now shows how to list all quarantined files with MpCmdRun in an elevated Command Prompt, followed by syntax for restoring a file.

2026-01-04.headline: Known-issues entry adds Google Workspace limits for Enterprise Edge protection and real-time DLP
2026-01-04.overview: Cloud Apps updates were concentrated in the known-issues guidance for Google Workspace in Enterprise Edge. The entry now documents unavailable in-browser protection, Secure Edge Session Controls, and real-time DLP file scans, with fallback authentication suffixes used instead of Secure Edge. A separate Asana setup step now specifies signing in with an admin account.
2026-01-04.adminImpact: Administrators planning Google Workspace access through Enterprise Edge should account for these documented protection and scanning limitations and the fallback authentication behavior. For Asana, the setup wording specifies an admin account; the supplied evidence identifies no separate remediation.

keyChanges.title: Google Workspace limitations documented for Enterprise Edge
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues entry states that Google Workspace does not support in-browser protection, Secure Edge Session Controls, or real-time DLP file scans in Enterprise Edge. Browser sessions use fallback authentication suffixes instead of Secure Edge.

keyChanges.title: Asana setup step specifies an admin account
keyChanges.detail: The Asana setup procedure now tells administrators to sign in to Asana with an admin account.

2026-01-05.headline: Live response eligibility and Salesforce connector prerequisites are clarified
2026-01-05.overview: The period’s most actionable guidance clarifies live response eligibility for Windows and legacy servers, adds a preparation checklist for the Salesforce connector, and expands Device Control troubleshooting. Controlled folder access guidance also now enumerates supported Windows and server paths, while several remaining edits mainly refresh links, labels, or release-note metadata.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: Review live response prerequisites before deployment or troubleshooting, especially on Windows Server 2012 R2 or 2016 and where static proxies are used. Use the Salesforce checklist to prepare the service account and permissions, verify controlled folder access against the operating system and deployment method, and use the expanded Device Control steps and current template source when troubleshooting or obtaining policy files.

keyChanges.title: Live response guidance now separates Windows and legacy-server requirements
keyChanges.detail: The page separates Windows 11 and Windows 10 support, reorganizes server requirements, and adds Windows Server 2012 R2 and 2016 details covering the Unified Agent, KB5005292, and a static-proxy limitation. Requirements for enabling live response and unsigned scripts are also clarified. Review these conditions before deployment or troubleshooting.

keyChanges.title: Salesforce connector setup gains a concrete administrator checklist
keyChanges.detail: The revised checklist covers the service admin account, REST API-supported Salesforce editions, required profile permissions, and conditional Salesforce CRM Content settings. Administrators can use it to prepare the connector account and permissions.

keyChanges.title: Controlled folder access guidance enumerates supported Windows paths
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now lists Windows 10 or later, Windows Server 2019 or later, and Windows Server 2016 and 2012 R2 through the modern unified Microsoft Defender for Endpoint solution. Use the operating system and deployment method to verify applicability.

keyChanges.title: Device Control FAQ expands media-device and access troubleshooting
keyChanges.detail: The FAQ adds explicit PowerShell formatting, expanded Device Manager steps for finding a media device instance path, updated Microsoft Entra group Object ID guidance, and clearer device-specific access requirements and screenshots. These additions support certificate validation, support-file collection, device identification, group mapping, and access diagnosis.

keyChanges.title: Device Control template downloads move to Microsoft Administrative Templates
keyChanges.detail: The FAQ changes the source for required .adml and .admx files from GitHub raw files to Microsoft Administrative Templates for Windows 10 2022 Update (22H2). It continues to state that Group Policy has no configuration UX for Device Control policy groups and rules.

2026-01-06.headline: Opt-in automatic Windows event auditing is coming to Defender for Identity unified sensors
2026-01-06.overview: The period's most consequential item is a Message Center rollout: Defender for Identity unified sensors v3.x will offer opt-in automatic Windows event-auditing configuration from mid-January 2026, with rollout completion expected by the end of January. Most other updates are documentation-led, but several have concrete setup implications for Endpoint and Identity administrators, plus least-privilege agent configuration and cloud-software exposure assessment.
2026-01-06.adminImpact: When available, enable automatic auditing through the Defender for Identity UI or Graph API if the deployment requires it. Also update firewall rules for the workspace-specific sensor URL, use the revised Endpoint network-protection workflow for older or high-UDP Windows Server roles, and follow the least-privilege identity guidance for the threat-intelligence briefing agent.

keyChanges.title: Unified sensors receive an opt-in automatic auditing option
keyChanges.detail: From mid-January 2026, Defender for Identity unified sensors v3.x will offer automatic configuration of Windows event-auditing settings. Administrators must enable the option through the UI or Graph API; rollout is scheduled to complete by the end of January.

keyChanges.title: Network protection guidance names roles, modes, and server limitations
keyChanges.detail: The updated Endpoint guidance uses the Endpoint Security Policies workflow, identifies the Security Administrator role as required, and documents the available network protection modes. It also covers downlevel settings for Windows Server 2012 R2 and 2016 and datagram-processing guidance for high-UDP server roles.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity sensor prerequisites now use a workspace-specific URL
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisites specify that network or firewall rules must allow `*<your-workspace-name>*sensorapi.atp.azure.com`, with an example of the required sensor URL format. Administrators should apply the applicable workspace name when updating allow rules.

keyChanges.title: Threat intelligence briefing agent guidance adopts a least-privilege setup
keyChanges.detail: The updated guide explains how to use a dedicated service-principal identity, links the configuration to Unified RBAC, and lists tenant-level administrator rights as a prerequisite for registering the identity and assigning roles.

keyChanges.title: Exposure Management guidance adds cloud-software inventory coverage
keyChanges.detail: The January Exposure Management content now documents cloud software inventory, including cloud software, application versions, installed assets, and related vulnerabilities. Administrators can use those details to understand exposure and prioritize vulnerability assessments.

2026-01-07.headline: Sentinel-backed near-real-time detection enters Microsoft Defender custom-rule preview
2026-01-07.overview: Microsoft Defender XDR’s January What's New entry records Near Real-Time configuration for custom detection rules using Microsoft Sentinel data, explicitly marked as preview. Other material administrator-facing changes include a narrower Vulnerability Management report model, clearer Device Discovery scan boundaries, deployment prerequisites for BehaviorEntities data, and a January Linux build with deeper React analysis. All 68 records were updates with none added or removed, so the period was primarily guidance and release-note maintenance rather than a broad product rollout.
2026-01-07.adminImpact: Treat the custom-rule Near Real-Time option as preview. For Vulnerability Management, account for the removed Windows 10/11 version-over-time section, Device group-only filtering, and 30-day history; government cloud customers are expected to see these changes in late January 2026. Device Discovery guidance now covers network-traffic and active-probing scans, exclusions, trusted networks, and the limitation that devices outside corporate networks are not discovered. BehaviorEntities queries depend on Defender for Cloud Apps and UEBA data; enable UEBA in Microsoft Sentinel and configure the documented Defender for Cloud Apps connection before relying on results. The Linux release entry states no required administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Custom detection rules document Near Real-Time Sentinel configuration in preview
keyChanges.detail: The Defender XDR January 2026 What's New entry says custom detection rules support Near Real-Time configuration for Microsoft Sentinel data and labels the capability as preview. Administrators can evaluate it for supported Sentinel data tables; no required action is stated.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Management removes report history and filtering options
keyChanges.detail: The updated What's New entry says the report removes the Windows 10/11 version-over-time section, limits filtering to Device group, and reduces history to the last 30 days. Government cloud customers are expected to see the changes in late January 2026.

keyChanges.title: Device Discovery clarifies scan coverage, onboarding, and network boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint guidance explains discovery through network traffic and active probing, how discovered devices are classified into inventory and can be onboarded, and how to configure scan modes, exclusions, trusted networks, and network scans. It also states that devices outside corporate networks are not discovered.

keyChanges.title: BehaviorEntities data depends on Defender for Cloud Apps and UEBA deployment
keyChanges.detail: The advanced hunting guidance now says Defender for Cloud Apps and UEBA populate the BehaviorEntities table; without those services deployed in Defender XDR, queries may fail or return no results. To populate records, administrators must enable UEBA in Microsoft Sentinel and follow the documented Defender for Cloud Apps connection steps.

keyChanges.title: Linux build adds deeper React analysis and CVE-2025-55182 telemetry
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Linux release entry dated January 7, 2026 identifies build 101.25102.0005 and documents deeper React component analysis plus enhanced telemetry, including identification of CVE-2025-55182. The update provides more visibility into vulnerabilities in React-based applications; no required action is stated.

2026-01-08.headline: Defender endpoint API guidance standardizes on `api.security.microsoft.com` across integration examples
2026-01-08.overview: The period’s most consequential update is a broad Endpoint API reference pass: documented request URLs, OData context and response links, and sample integrations replace `api.securitycenter.microsoft.com` with `api.security.microsoft.com`; one app-partner example also updates its resource URI and OAuth scope. Separately, Microsoft added Teams blocking guidance and made Unified SecOps onboarding prerequisites and guest limitations explicit. Most other supplied edits are formatting, navigation, terminology, or API-table cleanup.
2026-01-08.adminImpact: Review Defender for Endpoint scripts and integrations that copied the old host, and audit queries using API filter properties that are no longer listed. For Teams, check the documented roles, prerequisites, limits, and timing before applying domain or email blocks. For Unified SecOps, validate the Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 requirement for Unified RBAC, delegated access, and Azure B2B guest assumptions. No action is indicated for formatting-only edits.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint API references adopt the `api.security.microsoft.com` hostname
keyChanges.detail: Many Endpoint API reference pages now replace `api.securitycenter.microsoft.com` with `api.security.microsoft.com` in requests and OData examples. On the Get Machine Group Exposure Score page, both the GET endpoint and sample `@odata.context` URL changed; administrators maintaining scripts should update copied references.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Allow/Block List guidance now covers Teams domain blocking
keyChanges.detail: New guidance explains how to use the Tenant Allow/Block List to block domains and email addresses in Microsoft Teams. It documents prerequisites, roles, limits, expected timing, and the resulting impact: existing communications can be removed and new meetings, chats, channels, and calls blocked.

keyChanges.title: Unified SecOps onboarding adds Plan 2 and Azure B2B constraints
keyChanges.detail: The revised playbook combines environment preparation and customer onboarding, renumbers the sequence into three steps, and revises delegated-access guidance. It explicitly documents Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 as a prerequisite for Unified RBAC and records limitations for Azure B2B guests.

keyChanges.title: Security-baseline API documentation no longer lists id and CCE filters
keyChanges.detail: Get Security Baselines Assessment Configurations now links to OData guidance and examples and lists filtering on category and name; the previously displayed `id` and `CCE` filter properties are no longer shown. Review integrations that rely on those fields.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot pages add dedicated Threat Hunting and Dynamic Detection guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot Agents Defender page now includes sections for the Threat Hunting Agent and Dynamic Threat Detection Agent, with a link and screenshot for threat-hunting workflows. The additions make natural-language investigations and adaptive detection guidance easier to locate across Defender and Microsoft Sentinel.

2026-01-09.headline: Defender for Office 365 quarantine adds per-recipient listings and per-user release
2026-01-09.overview: The period’s clearest behavior change is the Defender for Office 365 quarantine rollout: beginning in January 2026 and completing by March, admin quarantine will list messages by individual recipient and require release per user. Backend durability is also being improved, with no end-user change. A new Teams Tenant Allow/Block List article supplies concrete blocking prerequisites and limits. The remaining updates are chiefly documentation maintenance covering mobile onboarding order, antivirus repair guidance, React telemetry wording, Core service scope, Plan 1 terminology, and Tenant Allow/Block List link cleanup, including removal of the former Teams configuration page.
2026-01-09.adminImpact: Update quarantine runbooks and administrative documentation for recipient-specific listings and per-user release. Before configuring Teams blocks, check the documented Teams settings, permissions, and limits of 4,000 domain entries and 200 user entries. Use the revised Antivirus startup procedure when troubleshooting and follow the documented app-installation and profile-assignment order for Intune mobile onboarding; no broader action is stated for the other reference updates.

keyChanges.title: Quarantine rollout changes administrator message handling
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the January 2026 rollout, completing by March, will list quarantined messages by individual recipient, improve backend durability, and require message release separately for each user. End-user behavior is unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Teams block-list guidance records prerequisites and entry limits
keyChanges.detail: The new article explains how security administrators block Teams domains and email addresses from the Microsoft Defender portal. It documents required Teams settings and permissions, limits of 4,000 domain entries and 200 user entries, and the effects and timing of blocking.

keyChanges.title: Mobile Threat Defense onboarding order is explicit for Intune enrollments
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance places Defender app installation and assignment of configuration profiles or policies before automatic onboarding, including for supervised ADE and Apple Configurator enrollments.

keyChanges.title: Antivirus startup troubleshooting adds repair steps and corrected paths
keyChanges.detail: The procedure now clarifies elevated command usage, updates MpCmdRun.exe paths, adds DISM and SFC repair commands, and revises the troubleshooting sequence and wording.

2026-01-10.headline: Safe Documents guidance names included A5, E5, G5, and Defender Suite licenses
2026-01-10.overview: The period brought two Office 365 documentation changes: a new reference for US government deployments and updated Safe Documents licensing guidance. The government page covers GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments, while the licensing page identifies included suites and excludes Defender for Office 365 Plans 1 and 2.
2026-01-10.adminImpact: Government administrators can use the new page to verify applicable licensing and portal or sensor endpoints for their environment. Administrators assessing Safe Documents eligibility should verify users have Microsoft 365 A5, E5, GCC G5, GCC High G5, or Microsoft Defender Suite licensing; Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2 do not include Safe Documents.

keyChanges.title: US government deployment coverage added
keyChanges.detail: A new Microsoft Learn page covers Microsoft Defender for Office 365 deployments in GCC, GCC High, and DoD, including licensing requirements, portal and sensor endpoints, and differences from the commercial offering.

keyChanges.title: Safe Documents service-plan eligibility specified
keyChanges.detail: The updated page lists Microsoft 365 A5, E5, GCC G5, GCC High G5, and Microsoft Defender Suite as products that include the SafeDocs service plan. It also states that Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2 do not include Safe Documents.

2026-01-11.headline: Defender Identity sensor v3 preview automates required Windows auditing settings
2026-01-11.overview: The most consequential update adds documented automatic auditing for Defender for Identity sensor v3.x: required Windows event settings are applied to new sensors and misconfigurations are corrected on existing domain controllers. Endpoint guidance now clarifies Device Discovery network handling and names supported Ubuntu Pro versions and architectures. In Unified SecOps, the 1,385-line MSSP technical playbook was removed while a separate implementation guide received navigation and link repairs.
2026-01-11.adminImpact: Identity administrators can use the automatic configuration capability or manually configure auditing through the Defender portal or PowerShell. Linux administrators should check deployments against the explicitly listed Ubuntu Pro 22.04 and 24.04 versions, including ARM64 variants. Device Discovery guidance now makes the consequences of monitoring non-corporate networks or ignoring networks clearer. MSSPs can no longer access the removed playbook at its listed URL, while the implementation guide's corrected sequence and links require no action.

keyChanges.title: Sensor v3.x guidance adds automatic Windows event auditing
keyChanges.detail: The Prerequisites Sensor Version 3 page now describes a preview capability that automatically applies required Windows event auditing settings to new sensors and fixes misconfigurations on existing domain controllers. Administrators can use the automatic configuration; otherwise, the documented alternative is manual configuration in the Defender portal or with PowerShell.

keyChanges.title: Device Discovery guidance details corporate-network monitoring and ignore effects
keyChanges.detail: The Configure Device Discovery guidance now explains default monitoring for corporate networks, consolidates network actions and their effects in a table, and updates filtering instructions. It also clarifies the risks of monitoring non-corporate networks and the stale inventory details that can result from ignoring networks.

keyChanges.title: MSSP technical playbook covering multitenant management was removed
keyChanges.detail: The 1,385-line Microsoft Defender Technical Playbook for MSSPs was deleted from the documentation site. The removed material included guidance for multitenant Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Sentinel management, and it is no longer available at the listed documentation URL.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint Linux prerequisites now name Ubuntu Pro versions and ARM64
keyChanges.detail: The MDE Linux prerequisites now list Ubuntu Pro 22.04 and 24.04, including their ARM64 variants, instead of generic Ubuntu Pro entries. Administrators should verify documented version and architecture coverage when assessing Linux deployments.

keyChanges.title: MSSP implementation guidance corrects links and the multitenant step sequence
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Defender portal implementation guide for MSSPs now uses corrected links, moves Multi-Tenant operations from Step 4 to Step 3, updates image paths, and adds service metadata. The changes improve navigation and document accuracy; no administrator action is required.

2026-01-12.headline: Defender device discovery guidance makes Standard scanning primary and flags Windows authenticated scan deprecation
2026-01-12.overview: The period was led by a substantial rewrite of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device discovery guidance. Standard scan is presented as the default, with clearer comparisons of scan behavior, protocols, use cases, exclusions, and probe traffic; the material also states that Windows authenticated scan is deprecated from 18 December 2025. Microsoft Defender for Identity guidance clarifies automatic auditing interactions with local policy and GPO files, while new Unified SecOps and Identity articles add coverage for MSSP onboarding and account linking. Most changes are documentation additions or revisions, with the scan deprecation statement and audit-policy instructions carrying the clearest planning implications.
2026-01-12.adminImpact: Endpoint teams still using Windows authenticated scans should review the deprecation FAQs and scan guidance against the documented 18 December 2025 date. For Defender for Identity automatic auditing, account for the domain controller’s local policy, remove conflicting audit.csv files from the local GPO store, and verify the running process as described. MSSPs can use the new implementation guide for customer onboarding and Sentinel workspace transitions; administrators using account-linking features need the Global Administrator or Security Data (Manage) URBAC role. Other listed changes are primarily reference, navigation, and terminology updates.

keyChanges.title: Standard discovery is now the documented default
keyChanges.detail: The Device Discovery guidance presents Standard scan first as the default, followed by Basic scan, and organizes the comparison around how each scan works, considerations, and use cases. Administrators can use the revised comparison when selecting a mode for their network protocols and conditions.

keyChanges.title: Windows authenticated scanning receives an explicit deprecation date
keyChanges.detail: The documentation describes authenticated network scans using designated onboarded Windows devices and read-only SNMPv2/v3 to discover network infrastructure, and states that Windows authenticated scan is deprecated from 18 December 2025. Administrators still using that path should review the deprecation FAQs and scan guidance.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity clarifies automatic auditing policy conflicts
keyChanges.detail: The Windows event collection guidance says automatic auditing applies settings to the domain controller’s local policy and warns that domain GPO audit.csv files can conflict. It adds verification through process checks, KQL, or auditpol; administrators using automatic configuration should remove conflicting audit.csv files from the local GPO store and verify the running process.

keyChanges.title: A new Unified SecOps guide structures MSSP onboarding
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Defender portal guide covers environment preparation, customer onboarding, content distribution, and daily multitenant security operations. It also highlights the need to transition Microsoft Sentinel workspaces when onboarding customers, giving MSSPs a reference for rollout planning and cross-tenant operations.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity documents cross-provider account linking
keyChanges.detail: A new article explains how to link or unlink legacy, orphaned, unused, and other related accounts across Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and non-Microsoft identity providers. Using the capability requires the Global Administrator or Security Data (Manage) URBAC role.

2026-01-13.headline: Live-response MDE tracing leads Defender guidance on connector and audit settings
2026-01-13.overview: The most actionable changes are administrator procedures rather than broad service announcements. A new Endpoint how-to documents MDE Client Analyzer tracing through live response; Cloud Apps guidance adds a reconfiguration step for connectors configured before January 2026; and Defender for Identity guidance adds a configuration report and Group Policy conflict check. Identity Inventory account linking and clearer Defender for Office 365 licensing guidance are also notable. Most other edits are terminology, links, schema, or page maintenance, including the Vulnerability Management shift from “vulnerable components” to “Software components.”
2026-01-13.adminImpact: For supported procedures, upload the latest analyzer package and enable live response before tracing; for Microsoft 365 connectors configured before January 2026, select all default components and choose Connect again, with file monitoring enabled for file protection; and run New-MDIConfigurationReport while reviewing Group Policy before automatic Windows event collection. Account linking requires the Global Administrator or Security Data (Manage) URBAC role. Use the explicit Plan 1 or Plan 2 eligibility wording when assessing access to the Teams message entity panel.

keyChanges.title: New Endpoint runbook documents live-response MDE tracing
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to explains how to start and stop MDE Client Analyzer tracing on supported Windows devices through live response. The procedure requires live response to be enabled and the latest analyzer package uploaded, then covers verifying collection, reproducing an issue, and stopping the trace. It supports troubleshooting when users are signed out or direct device access is restricted.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Apps guidance adds a January 2026 connector reconfiguration step
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps guidance now says all Microsoft 365 components are selected by default for maximum protection. Required components support certain detection and response functions, while file protection still requires file monitoring. For connectors configured before January 2026, administrators should select all default options and choose Connect again.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity adds a preflight report to event-collection guidance
keyChanges.detail: Configure Windows Event Collection now recommends running New-MDIConfigurationReport before configuration and describes sensor-applied auditing changes for directory services, NTLM, domain objects, AD FS, and Windows audit policies. It also warns that Group Policy can conflict with sensor-applied local settings, so administrators should review existing policies before enabling automatic collection.

keyChanges.title: Identity Inventory gets account linking with explicit URBAC roles
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to explains how to link or unlink legacy, unused, and orphaned accounts to identities through the Defender portal’s Identity Inventory. The documented roles are Global Administrator or Security Data (Manage).

keyChanges.title: Teams message panel eligibility guidance now names Plan 1 and Plan 2
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Defender for Office 365 guidance now states that the Teams message entity panel is available to organizations with Plan 1 and Plan 2, replacing wording that described Plan 2 only. Plan 1 administrators can use the updated eligibility guidance when assessing access.

2026-01-14.headline: Endpoint DLP alerting retires in March as Defender for Identity automates auditing
2026-01-14.overview: The period was dominated by Endpoint documentation maintenance, including removal of legacy Tech Community references. The substantive administrator changes are a March retirement of endpoint-sensitive-data alerting, a required path for new macOS extension policies, an automatic Defender for Identity auditing rollout, clarified Unified RBAC role guidance, and a planned Cloud Apps connector configuration update.
2026-01-14.adminImpact: Prioritize moving endpoint-sensitive-data alerting, enforcement, and investigation to Microsoft Purview DLP before 23 March 2026. Use the Intune settings catalog for new macOS extension policies; no migration is stated for existing policies. Monitor Defender for Identity health alerts during the auditing rollout, apply the clarified Unified RBAC guidance when evaluating activation, and review Cloud Apps connector settings and required Entra permissions when the planned page update arrives.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint DLP sensitive-data alerting has a March 23 retirement deadline
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft will retire endpoint-sensitive-data alerting in the Microsoft Defender portal by 23 March 2026. Existing Defender alert policies will stop generating alerts after that date; Microsoft directs organizations to Microsoft Purview DLP for endpoint alerting, enforcement, and investigation.
keyChanges.product: Defender XDR and Microsoft Purview DLP

keyChanges.title: New macOS extension policies must use the Intune settings catalog
keyChanges.detail: The guidance records that Intune policy support for creating macOS extension policies was deprecated in the August 2024 service release 2048. Existing policies continue to work, while new policies must use the settings catalog and configure the System Extension payload; no migration is stated for existing policies.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity rolls out automatic auditing correction for v3.x sensors
keyChanges.detail: During the gradual rollout, required Windows event-auditing settings are applied to new version 3.x sensors and misconfigurations are corrected on existing sensors. Related health alerts identify auditing problems; administrators should understand the automatic behavior and monitor those alerts.

keyChanges.title: Unified RBAC guidance now names Security Administrators as retaining privileges
keyChanges.detail: The Manage RBAC guidance now says Security Administrators retain their assigned administrator privileges when Microsoft Defender XDR Unified RBAC is activated, replacing the previous reference to Global Administrators. The revised wording should be used when evaluating activation; no required action is stated.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Apps connector updates add defaults for new Microsoft 365 connectors
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the Microsoft 365 connector configuration page will receive clearer layouts and new default values for new connectors in January 2026. Existing connectors remain unchanged; administrators should review current settings and confirm that required Entra permissions are enabled.

2026-01-15.headline: Teams ZAP unavailable across GCC, GCC High, and DoD as setup guidance sharpens
2026-01-15.overview: The clearest administrator-facing change is an explicit scope limit for Zero-hour Auto Purge in Teams: the guidance says it is unavailable in Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, and DoD. Other substantive updates tighten macOS System Extension profile instructions, consolidate Windows EDR detection testing around a TCP port 80 prerequisite, document partial Defender XDR query results above 64 MB, and record removal of telemetryd_v2 in Linux builds 101.25102.0005 and later. Most remaining edits are feedback, metadata, link, screenshot, or terminology maintenance.
2026-01-15.adminImpact: Administrators in the affected government clouds should not expect Teams ZAP protection. macOS profile authors should use the Intune Settings Catalog guidance, EDR test operators should verify TCP port 80 when required, and XDR query users should treat over-limit results as partial. The Linux update requires no administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Teams ZAP scope excludes GCC, GCC High, and DoD
keyChanges.detail: The Zero Hour Auto Purge guidance now states that Zero-hour Auto Purge for Microsoft Teams isn't available in Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, or DoD.

keyChanges.title: Intune macOS profiles specify System Extension settings
keyChanges.detail: The article now directs administrators to the Intune Settings Catalog for Allowed System Extensions and Allowed System Extension Types, including the required bundle identifiers, extension types, and team identifier.

keyChanges.title: EDR detection testing consolidates Windows prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: Separate Windows client and server sections are replaced by one Windows section, client-specific PowerShell test steps are removed, and the TCP port 80 prerequisite applies to the Windows device.

keyChanges.title: Defender XDR identifies query results above 64 MB as partial
keyChanges.detail: When query results exceed 64 MB, the portal returns the maximum number of records that fit and displays a message explaining that the results are partial.

keyChanges.title: Linux builds remove the dedicated telemetryd_v2 process
keyChanges.detail: For builds 101.25102.0005 and later, agent process handling is streamlined by removing telemetryd_v2 while preserving existing functionality and data collection.

2026-01-16.headline: Windows local onboarding guidance recommends scripts for 10 devices or fewer
2026-01-16.overview: All 14 entries were documentation updates, with no new or removed items. The most consequential guidance concerns Windows onboarding scale, Defender Antivirus registry verification after updates, and the documented Linux telemetryd_v2 build threshold. Office 365 also added a license-based Teams protection matrix, while Defender RBAC guidance explicitly includes Microsoft Sentinel.
2026-01-16.adminImpact: Use the local onboarding script for 10 devices or fewer; use other deployment methods for production or larger deployments, following the revised portal, connectivity, and elevated-command-prompt steps. After Defender Antivirus platform or engine updates, verify relevant registry keys and update them manually if needed. Use the Teams matrix for license comparisons and build 101.24062.0001 as the documented Linux telemetryd_v2 threshold.

keyChanges.title: Local onboarding script guidance is set at 10 devices or fewer
keyChanges.detail: The Windows local-script article now recommends this method for 10 devices or fewer, advises other deployment methods for production or larger deployments, and updates the Defender portal path, Standard and Streamlined connectivity choices, and elevated-command-prompt procedure.

keyChanges.title: Defender Antivirus warns that registry entries may lag platform updates
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now says some registry entries may not update automatically after the latest Defender Antivirus platform or engine update. Administrators should verify the relevant keys and update them manually if needed so they reflect the current version.

keyChanges.title: Teams protection coverage is mapped across license levels
keyChanges.detail: The Teams security article now includes a matrix covering all Teams licenses, Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, and Plan 2. The matrix includes Safe Links, Safe Attachments, quarantine, remediation, attack simulation training, and advanced hunting.

keyChanges.title: Linux telemetryd_v2 removal is tied to build 101.24062.0001 and later
keyChanges.detail: The documented threshold changed from build 101.25102.0005 and later to 101.24062.0001 and later. The article states that existing functionality and data collection are unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Defender RBAC guidance explicitly includes Microsoft Sentinel

2026-08-05.headline: Teams adds default-on reporting for suspicious meetings and group calls
2026-08-05.overview: The period’s most consequential updates are two Microsoft Teams reporting capabilities tied to Defender XDR. Meeting reporting starts in August 2026, while group-call reporting rolls out from August through October; both are enabled by default. An Endpoint documentation update also clarifies how Intune represents Defender Antivirus update-source priority.
2026-08-05.adminImpact: Defender XDR administrators should expect user-submitted reports from Teams meetings and group calls to be reviewable in Teams admin center and Microsoft Defender, supporting security investigations. For Endpoint policy configuration, Intune administrators can use the clarified prioritized-list view to set the fallback order for Defender Antivirus update sources.

keyChanges.title: Teams meeting reporting starts in August
keyChanges.detail: Users will be able to report suspicious or malicious activity during Teams meetings. Reports support investigation through Microsoft Defender and Teams admin center, with the feature enabled by default and administrative controls and investigation-related data collection included.

keyChanges.title: Group-call reporting rolls out through October
keyChanges.detail: Users will be able to report suspicious calls from call history. The capability is enabled by default and rolls out from August through October 2026; administrators can review reports in Teams admin center and Microsoft Defender.

keyChanges.title: Intune guidance clarifies Defender Antivirus update-source ordering
keyChanges.detail: The underlying policy uses a pipe-separated string, while Intune presents the setting as a prioritized list of update sources. Administrators can use that list to configure the desired fallback order.

2026-08-10.headline: Safe Links warnings from pinned Teams tabs now open in new tabs

2026-08-10.adminImpact: Administrators should expect a different user experience when users access flagged links from pinned Teams tabs. The update states no administrator action or configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Safe Links warning-page behavior is specified for pinned Teams tabs
keyChanges.detail: The updated Safe Links guidance says the warning page opens in a new browser tab when a user clicks a flagged link from a pinned Teams tab, rather than appearing within the Teams tab.

2026-08-11.headline: macOS Defender troubleshooting adds process-specific diagnostics and safer exclusion guidance
2026-08-11.overview: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on macOS received a focused troubleshooting guidance refresh. The updates add targeted workflows for high resource use, Network Extension failures, and system extension problems, while clarifying that antivirus exclusions do not suppress EDR or other Endpoint Security events.
2026-08-11.adminImpact: Use the new diagnostics before changing exclusions or disabling components. For performance issues, collect data while the problem occurs and check the specific Defender process or workload involved. Test NetExt changes with a small pilot and restore the original configuration afterward; review macOS MDM payload structure when investigating system extension issues.

keyChanges.title: Performance guidance now targets wdavdaemon and wdavdaemon_enterprise
keyChanges.detail: The performance workflow adds Activity Monitor or top checks, hot-event-source collection, Client Analyzer data, coexistence checks, and support information for persistent high resource use. It also states that antivirus exclusions do not suppress EDR or other Endpoint Security events, so broad exclusions may not address the cause.

keyChanges.title: Exclusion guidance maps workloads to narrower troubleshooting steps
keyChanges.detail: The exclusions article now maps affected Defender processes and workloads to recommended next steps and advises validating CPU, memory, scan counts, and elapsed time after an exclusion is applied. Administrators are cautioned to avoid broad exclusions and remove exclusions that do not improve the measured issue.

keyChanges.title: NetExt troubleshooting separates Network Protection from general NetExt failures
keyChanges.detail: The revised workflow distinguishes enforcement problems in Network Protection from issues that occur whenever NetExt runs. It adds health checks, a test matrix, diagnostic commands, and information to collect, while warning that disabling NetExt reduces network visibility and disables dependent capabilities.

keyChanges.title: System extension guidance adds MDM payload and profile checks
keyChanges.detail: Administrators are directed to review profiles under System Settings > General > Device Management, deploy each Defender for Endpoint configuration as a separate payload, and use the updated profile-analysis command when diagnosing system extension issues.

keyChanges.title: The macOS troubleshooting overview now emphasizes data collection during failures
keyChanges.detail: The overview adds process-specific troubleshooting steps and recommends collecting performance data while the issue is occurring. It reiterates that antivirus exclusions do not exclude EDR or other security event processing, helping administrators avoid using exclusions for the wrong Defender component.

2026-08-25.headline: Defender XDR adds unified identity actions and a consolidated timeline this fall
2026-08-25.overview: Two Defender XDR identity-protection announcements set out a fall 2026 rollout: centralized response actions across linked identities, followed by a richer Identity-page timeline that combines activity and alerts from Microsoft security sources.
2026-08-25.adminImpact: The unified timeline requires no enablement action and does not change existing policies. It will roll out from mid-September through mid-October 2026. keyChanges.title: Unified response actions across identity accounts

keyChanges.title: Identity page receives a unified Timeline
keyChanges.detail: The Identity page’s Timeline tab will show a chronological view of identity-related activities and alerts from multiple Microsoft security sources, with improved context, filtering, and automatic updates. Rollout is planned from mid-September through mid-October 2026; no action is required to enable it, and existing policies are unchanged.

2026-08-26.headline: App Governance retires Cloud Application Administrator support on September 26
2026-08-26.overview: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps will retire App Governance support for the Cloud Application Administrator role on September 26, 2026. The change affects organizations using URBAC and requires role assignments to be reviewed before the cutoff.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Application Administrator support is being retired
keyChanges.detail: App Governance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps will no longer support the Cloud Application Administrator role after September 26, 2026. keyChanges.title: AIR is integrated into always-on antivirus
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is moving AIR functions into always-on antivirus protection and removing the standalone AIR experience by early September 2026. Manual triggering will also be removed.

2026-09-02.headline: Defender for Office 365 will quarantine AI-targeting prompt injections by default
2026-09-02.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is preparing prompt injection protection for email, with rollout scheduled from July through October 2026 for organizations with Defender Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5. The remaining updates are targeted guidance and documentation corrections: Defender XDR now specifies required device identifiers for Sentinel-mapped activity, Defender for Identity documents custom service-account classification, and Endpoint troubleshooting corrects a registry-path typo.
2026-09-02.adminImpact: No action is required for the email protection rollout. Administrators ingesting custom Sentinel activity should verify the required device-identifier combinations; Identity administrators can use custom classification rules to identify service accounts missed by automatic detection. The Endpoint change provides the accurate registry path for troubleshooting and requires no corrective action.

keyChanges.title: Prompt injection protection planned for email
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will detect and quarantine malicious email content targeting AI assistants. For organizations with Defender Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5, automatic high-confidence threat quarantine is enabled by default during the July–October 2026 rollout, with no required administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Device Timeline mappings require specific identifiers
keyChanges.detail: The Entity Page guidance now specifies that custom activity data mapped from Sentinel to Microsoft Defender XDR must include either HostName plus NTDomain or HostName plus DnsDomain for correct Device Timeline visibility.

keyChanges.title: Custom rules can identify missed service accounts
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Identity guidance explains that custom classification rules can identify service accounts not detected automatically, including accounts using an `srv` prefix.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint troubleshooting path corrected
keyChanges.detail: The troubleshooting guidance corrects the `ProductAppDataPath` registry value from `Microsft` to `Microsoft` in the Windows Defender data path, giving administrators the accurate registry path to use when following the procedure.

2026-09-03.headline: Secure Score will add four AI-readiness checks for device security
2026-09-03.overview: The period’s main product-facing change is a Microsoft Secure Score rollout for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Four recommendations covering TPM 2.0, VBS, HVCI, and LAPS will roll out from early to late September 2026. Most other activity was documentation maintenance, with useful exceptions covering connectivity allowlists, missing Threat Analytics reports, and isolation behavior.
2026-09-03.adminImpact: No action is required to receive the new Secure Score recommendations. Administrators configuring Defender connectivity should review Microsoft 365 Unified Domains, while incident responders should check Threat intelligence for missing emailed reports and review isolation exclusions when automatic attack disruption causes full isolation.

keyChanges.title: Secure Score adds four device-security readiness recommendations
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Secure Score will add four AI-readiness recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, covering TPM 2.0, VBS, HVCI, and LAPS. They will roll out from early to late September 2026 and help identify and remediate devices lacking those protections; no action is required to receive them.

keyChanges.title: Device connectivity allowlists may require Microsoft 365 Unified Domains
keyChanges.detail: The commercial standard device-connectivity guidance now says that some environments may need to allow URLs from the Microsoft 365 unified domains list in addition to the URLs in the existing table. Review the linked list when configuring or validating network allowlists.

keyChanges.title: Missing emailed Threat Analytics reports may be in Threat intelligence
keyChanges.detail: The Threat Analytics guidance now directs administrators to check the Threat intelligence section when an emailed threat analytics report is missing from Threat analytics.

keyChanges.title: Automatic attack disruption can result in full isolation
keyChanges.detail: The response guidance now notes that the issue can occur when automatic attack disruption triggers full isolation. Administrators can define an isolation exclusion rule to use selective isolation instead.

keyChanges.title: Custom detection rules correct the ABAP audit table name
keyChanges.detail: The supported table list now spells `ABAPAuditLog_CL` correctly, fixing the missing “L.” Administrators referencing ABAP audit log data should use the corrected table name when creating custom detection rules.

2026-09-04.headline: Sentinel table migration and Linux enforcement changes sharpen administrator action
2026-09-04.overview: The period was dominated by documentation maintenance, but several updates carry direct operational weight. Sentinel guidance now points administrators from the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table to ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects, while Defender for Endpoint documents four Linux antivirus enforcement levels, a passive default, and Preview audit mode. Other consequential changes include SIEM-agent deprecation guidance for the Cloud Apps integration, manual Preview activation limits for Defender for Identity v3.x sensors on non-domain controllers, and material changes to the documented Defender XDR DataSecurityEvents schema.
2026-09-04.adminImpact: Prioritize any remaining Sentinel content that depends on the legacy threat-intelligence table, then review Linux enforcement profiles and version requirements. Administrators using SIEM agents with Defender for Cloud Apps should reassess the supported Sentinel integration path. Identity teams deploying v3.x sensors on AD FS, AD CS, or Microsoft Entra Connect servers must account for manual activation and the requirement for at least one domain-controller sensor. Hunting and integration owners should check DataSecurityEvents queries for documented column removals.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel threat-intelligence content must move off the legacy table
keyChanges.detail: The STIX guidance directs content to the ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects schemas and states that ingestion into the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table stops after July 31, 2025. Custom queries, analytics and detection rules, workbooks, and automation using the old table should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Linux antivirus enforcement now has four documented levels
keyChanges.detail: The Linux configuration article lists four antivirus enforcement levels, identifies passive as the default, and marks audit mode as Preview. It adds verification guidance for the active level; audit mode requires Defender for Endpoint version 101.26062.0007 or later.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Apps integration guidance now deprecates SIEM agents
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel integration page states that SIEM agents are deprecated while the Microsoft Sentinel integration (Preview) remains supported, and adds a dedicated integration section. Organizations still using SIEM agents should review their integration strategy against the supported Sentinel option.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity documents manual v3.x activation on additional servers
keyChanges.detail: The v3.x sensor deployment guidance now covers non-domain-controller AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers. Activation on those servers is in Preview and requires manual activation; automatic activation and migration are unsupported. Deployments limited to these servers should include at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller.

keyChanges.title: DataSecurityEvents reference adds and removes hunting columns
keyChanges.detail: The Defender XDR table reference removes its Preview and prerelease notices, adds physical access, removable media, and risky AI usage fields, and removes several URL, email, file-path, workload, and Cloud App Alert fields. Query and integration owners should review dependencies on the removed columns.

2026-09-08.headline: Sentinel parser guidance forbids cross-table enrichment and preserves one output per source record
2026-09-08.overview: The day’s most consequential updates sharpen Sentinel parser guidance and revise the documented severity of seven Azure Storage alerts to Informational. Defender XDR added dedicated guidance for mapping Advanced Hunting results into graphs, while Defender for Identity added resolution steps for the Sensor v3.x RPC Audit Misconfigured health alert. The remaining edits are primarily layout, link, terminology, and explanatory maintenance.
2026-09-08.adminImpact: Review custom Sentinel parsers and connectors against the declared source-table, one-output-per-record, and mapping restrictions. Source filtering must use fields in the current event, with missing source information addressed in the connector or source-specific table. Use the revised Informational labels when reviewing the seven documented Azure Storage alerts, and verify Unified Sensor RPC Audit configuration when troubleshooting the Identity health alert. Advanced Hunting teams can use the new graph-mapping guidance for query-result preparation and enrichment.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel parser guidance sets strict source and cardinality boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The updated normalization guidance limits parsers to the declared source table, requires one normalized output per source record, and permits scalar or local static mappings. It explicitly prohibits cross-table enrichment, watchlists, multi-value expansion, joins, aggregation, and deduplication. Source filtering must use fields in the current event; missing source information should be handled in the connector or source-specific table.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel parser-creation guidance permits lookup mappings only with unique keys
keyChanges.detail: The parser-creation skills guidance says each source record is normalized independently and record cardinality is preserved. Query-local datatable or lookup mappings are allowed when lookup keys are unique, while same-table and cross-table event enrichment are not used.

keyChanges.title: New Defender XDR guidance details graph mapping for Advanced Hunting
keyChanges.detail: The new guide explains how to prepare query results, configure graph nodes and edges, apply relationship conditions, and use recognized entity types and identifiers for Defender enrichment.

keyChanges.title: Azure Storage alert documentation now labels seven entries Informational
keyChanges.detail: Seven documented Azure Storage alert entries now list their severity as Informational instead of High, Medium, or Low variants. Administrators reviewing the alert reference should use the revised labels when prioritizing those entries.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity adds resolution steps for an RPC audit health alert
keyChanges.detail: The health-issues article now includes resolution guidance for the Sensor v3.x RPC Audit Misconfigured entry, including verification of the Unified Sensor RPC Audit configuration.

2026-09-18.headline: Advanced Hunting adds MessageContents table for Teams message investigations
2026-09-18.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is introducing a new MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting for Microsoft Teams messages. Authorized security analysts will be able to query message snippets and metadata for threat investigations, with worldwide rollout scheduled from late September through mid-October 2026.
2026-09-18.adminImpact: Account for the worldwide rollout window and ensure authorized analysts have the appropriate permissions to access the new table.

keyChanges.title: New Teams message hunting data
keyChanges.detail: The MessageContents table adds queryable snippets and metadata from Microsoft Teams messages to Advanced Hunting for threat investigations. Access requires appropriate permissions, and rollout is planned worldwide from late September to mid-October 2026.

2026-09-21.headline: Teams message flyout will combine Microsoft submission and sender blocking by late September
2026-09-21.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will enhance the Teams message entity flyout by late September 2026. Security admins will be able to submit messages to Microsoft and block senders or domains within one workflow, covering Plan 1 and Plan 2 customers without configuration changes.
2026-09-21.adminImpact: Admins investigating Teams messages should expect a consolidated remediation workflow by late September 2026. No configuration changes are required.

keyChanges.title: Teams message entity flyout gains remediation actions
keyChanges.detail: The enhanced flyout will let security admins submit a Teams message to Microsoft and block its sender or domain from the same workflow. The change is planned for late September 2026 and applies to Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2 customers.

2026-09-28.headline: Defender for Endpoint distinguishes cloned Linux VMs and avoids SSE4.1 crashes
2026-09-28.overview: The period contained one Endpoint update: cloned Linux virtual machines are now correctly identified as unique Defender for Endpoint devices, while SIGILL crashes on processors without SSE4.1 support were fixed. The update also includes general reliability improvements.
2026-09-28.adminImpact: No administrator action is stated. Affected Linux deployments should experience more accurate device identification and improved stability.

keyChanges.title: Linux device identity and stability fixes
keyChanges.detail: Cloned Linux virtual machines are now correctly identified as unique Defender for Endpoint devices. SIGILL crashes on processors without SSE4.1 support were fixed, along with general reliability improvements.

2026-09-29.headline: Defender for Identity sensor v3 guidance adds tenant, update, and activation checks
2026-09-29.overview: Most updates were editorial or procedural, but the consequential guidance centered on Defender for Identity sensor v3 deployment and migration. Administrators now have explicit prerequisites for sensor 3.0.8 and later, a cross-tenant migration limitation, and details about automatic activation and Windows auditing. New guidance also covers direct Microsoft Entra RBAC assignments to service principals in Defender for Cloud Apps and Azure Government publishing for Sentinel CCF solutions.
2026-09-29.adminImpact: Before deploying or upgrading sensor v3, validate the Windows Server patch level, tenant alignment, and server eligibility. Review the Sensor management notice if automatic activation is offered and opt out if appropriate. Cloud Apps administrators can use the new service-principal RBAC guidance after confirming app governance access and role prerequisites; Sentinel solution publishers targeting Azure Government should validate Partner Center settings and government-cloud connector endpoints.

keyChanges.title: Sensor 3.0.8 and later requires a July 2026-or-later Windows Server update
keyChanges.detail: The Deploy Sensor V3 guidance requires a July 2026 or later Windows Server cumulative update before installing or upgrading to sensor version 3.0.8 or later for automatic RPC auditing on domain controllers. Manual activation preview remains limited to eligible non-domain-controller AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers without an existing sensor.

keyChanges.title: Cross-tenant sensor v2.x-to-v3.x migration is unsupported
keyChanges.detail: The troubleshooting guidance states that migration fails when the Defender for Identity workspace and Defender for Endpoint onboarding for the same server belong to different Microsoft tenants. The server may appear ready, but sensor v3.x activation fails.

keyChanges.title: Automatic sensor activation guidance now covers eligible non-domain controllers
keyChanges.detail: The updated What's New guidance says eligible new Defender for Endpoint customers may receive automatic Defender for Identity sensor v3.x activation and Windows auditing. Existing Defender for Identity customers receive a portal notice before these settings are enabled, and eligible non-domain-controller AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers are covered.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Apps adds a playbook for direct Entra RBAC roles on service principals
keyChanges.detail: New guidance shows how to use Defender for Cloud Apps app governance to filter, investigate, and assess Microsoft Entra RBAC roles assigned directly to service principals, including role permissions, privilege levels, and risk signals. Access to app governance data and the required app governance role are prerequisites.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel publishers get Azure Government guidance for CCF solutions
keyChanges.detail: A new guide covers prerequisites, Partner Center publishing, and Azure Government endpoint updates for Sentinel CCF data connector solutions. Publishers targeting Azure Government should provide the corresponding government-cloud values and validate connector endpoints to help prevent connection failures.

2026-09-30.headline: Foundational CSPM will default off for new Azure subscriptions October 27
2026-09-30.overview: The main operational change is a Defender for Cloud default-setting shift: Foundational CSPM will remain free but will no longer be enabled automatically for new Azure subscriptions from October 27, 2026. Related updates clarify Defender for Servers billing treatment, while Defender for Office 365 is adding email-submission data to Advanced Hunting. Office 365 guidance also tightens the documented format for Punycode URLs.
2026-09-30.adminImpact: Add an explicit Foundational CSPM enablement step when provisioning new Azure subscriptions if the plan is required. Reassess Defender for Servers cost estimates for device classification, per-machine counting, and VMs in the Starting power state. Hunting teams can prepare for the new tables, but Microsoft states that no immediate action or compliance change is required. Review Punycode entries in Tenant Allow/Block List configurations against the documented hostname format.

keyChanges.title: Foundational CSPM default changes for new Azure subscriptions
keyChanges.detail: Starting October 27, 2026, Foundational CSPM will no longer be enabled by default for new Azure subscriptions. The plan remains free and can be enabled at any time; existing subscriptions and AWS or GCP environments are unaffected.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Servers revises device classification and server counting
keyChanges.detail: Plan 1 will no longer bill desktop, workstation, and mobile devices as servers. For Plans 1 and 2, server identification will run more frequently and count deployed machines individually, which may change billed server totals.

keyChanges.title: Starting-state VMs are included in Defender for Servers billing guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Servers FAQ now states that virtual machines in the Starting power state are billed and links to upcoming billing updates. Administrators should include these VMs when estimating costs.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting adds email submission telemetry tables
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will add the SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults Advanced Hunting tables, rolling out worldwide in early October 2026. They provide enhanced visibility into email submissions and support tailored detection workflows; no immediate action or compliance change is required.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Allow/Block List guidance limits Unicode and Punycode URL formats
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now states that Unicode is unsupported and that Punycode is allowed only in hostname labels before a normal ASCII top-level domain. Configured Punycode URLs should follow that format.

2026-10-01.headline: Central Linux scans and Teams reporting controls get sharper Defender administrator guidance
2026-10-01.overview: The substantive 1 October updates are mostly documentation guidance, but several now pin down settings and behaviors relevant to administrators. Endpoint guidance covers centrally scheduled Linux antivirus scans and clarifies secure-configuration scope; Defender for Office 365 provides more precise Teams reporting setup; Sentinel references add connector and table support details. Most of the remaining Defender for Business changes refresh navigation, terminology, and procedures.
2026-10-01.adminImpact: Review the secure-configuration guidance if you manage Windows Server 2022 or 2025, or local antivirus exclusions. Use the updated Teams reporting and Sentinel references when configuring those services, and consult the Linux release guidance if centrally scheduled scans are required. Most other Business updates are navigational or wording improvements with no action stated.

keyChanges.title: Secure configuration guidance adds Windows Server 2022 and 2025
keyChanges.detail: The updated Endpoint guidance now includes Windows Server 2022 and Windows Server 2025 in the device requirement. It also states that local administrator-defined antivirus exclusions are not honored by default and can be enabled through Defender or Intune policy.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint release guidance documents centrally scheduled Linux antivirus scans
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Defender Endpoint Releases page now documents centrally scheduled Linux antivirus scans through managed JSON and Defender Portal policies. It also adds release information covering detection of critical Node.js, Python, and Java libraries, the libcurl 8.20.0 security update, and Windows Antivirus August 2026-2 fixes.

keyChanges.title: Teams reporting setup gains explicit portal and PowerShell destinations
keyChanges.detail: The updated Teams submissions guidance points administrators to the Teams user reported settings page and provides Exchange Online PowerShell commands for viewing and configuring report destinations: Microsoft, a reporting mailbox, or both.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel connector references add Meraki File Scanned data and DCR support
keyChanges.detail: The Cisco Meraki connector reference now documents File Scanned detections and the `CiscoMerakiFileScannedEvents_CL` table. It also marks the F5Telemetry LTM and RFI Playbook Alert Results tables as supported and documents workspace transform DCR support.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Business clarifies which policy takes effect
keyChanges.detail: The revised policy-order guidance states that only the highest-priority applicable policy is applied. Default policy priority remains fixed; newly created policies receive a priority, and moving them changes the position of default policies.

2026-10-02.headline: Defender for Office 365 rolls out promotional-mail tagging and automatic folder moves
2026-10-02.overview: Defender for Office 365 will label promotional emails as “promotions” and can move them automatically to a Promotions folder, learning from user actions. Separately, the Office 365 permissions documentation removes the “related to Copilot” qualifier from descriptions of Data Security AI Admin DLP permissions while retaining the exclusion for prompt and response access.
2026-10-02.adminImpact: Administrators control the promotional-mail settings, while users can customize handling by moving messages. The Message Center timeline places public preview in mid-April 2026 and completion of general rollout in late 2026. No action is required for the permissions wording update; administrators should use the revised descriptions when reviewing or communicating role permissions.

keyChanges.title: Promotional emails gain “promotions” labels and automatic folder handling
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Defender for Office 365 will tag promotional emails as “promotions” and can automatically move them to a Promotions folder. The capability learns from user actions, and users can customize handling by moving messages. Public preview starts in mid-April 2026, with general rollout completing by late 2026.

keyChanges.title: Data Security AI Admin descriptions remove the Copilot qualifier
keyChanges.detail: The Scc Permissions page now describes Data Security AI Admins and the Data Security AI Admin role as able to edit Data Loss Prevention policies without the previous “related to Copilot” qualifier. It continues to document access to view AI content, while prompt and response access remains excluded.

2026-10-04.headline: Custom detections spell out 5-minute-to-14-day scheduling and lookback boundaries
2026-10-04.overview: The period focuses on guidance changes that sharpen administrator decisions. Custom-detection pages spell out the 5-minute-to-14-day custom-frequency range, the Sentinel-only data-source boundary, fixed 4-hour-to-30-day lookbacks for Defender XDR data, and Sentinel lookback limits that remain in public preview. Other meaningful updates clarify Unified RBAC coverage for identity exclusions, restrict two Cloud Apps admin roles in new configurations, and record four GA Defender for Cloud sensor builds with security and dependency fixes.
2026-10-04.adminImpact: When creating or reviewing custom detections, verify the data source and applicable lookback rules. For identity exclusions, confirm Unified RBAC assignments cover the relevant Defender for Identity and Defender for Endpoint data sources. Existing Cloud Apps role assignments remain supported, but they cannot be used in new configurations; Microsoft Support is the stated route if those capabilities are needed. Use the Defender for Cloud sensor entries for version and security tracking; no required action is stated.

keyChanges.title: Custom frequency is restricted to Sentinel-only detections
keyChanges.detail: Updated Custom Detection Rules guidance says custom frequency from 5 minutes to 14 days is available only for rules based exclusively on Microsoft Sentinel data. Rules using Defender XDR data instead use fixed lookback periods tied to run frequency, ranging from 4 hours to 30 days, and cannot use custom scoping with this frequency option.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel guidance sets preview lookback ceilings by frequency
keyChanges.detail: The comparison guidance lists flexible and high-frequency support for Sentinel data: lookback is up to 48 hours when frequency exceeds one hour and up to 14 days when frequency is one hour or less. Lookback remains labeled public preview.

keyChanges.title: Identity-exclusion guidance covers both response products
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains that identity exclusions affect automated response actions in both Defender for Identity and Defender for Endpoint. Its Unified RBAC permissions coverage now addresses both products’ data sources, role assignments, and data-source scope.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Apps admin roles are unavailable for new configurations
keyChanges.detail: App/instance admin and User group admin role assignments can no longer be used in new configurations. Existing configurations remain supported, and organizations needing these capabilities are directed to Microsoft Support.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud records four September GA sensor builds
keyChanges.detail: The sensor changelog now lists versions 0.11.7, 0.10.10, 0.9.68, and 0.8.61 as September 2026 GA releases, each containing security vulnerability fixes and dependency updates.

2026-10-05.headline: Defender for Cloud Apps will auto-enable Identity inventory for eligible tenants October 15
2026-10-05.overview: Starting October 15, 2026, the Defender for Cloud Apps integration with Identity inventory will move from opt-in to automatic enablement for eligible tenants without listed excluded configurations. Defender for Storage adds targeted on-demand scanning, while Defender for Cloud guidance adds integration prerequisites and Linux requirements. Microsoft also documents the Defender XDR Hunts experience for Defender Experts customers and clarifies Identity sensor v3 activation eligibility and operating mode.
2026-10-05.adminImpact: Eligible Cloud Apps tenants should prepare for automatic Identity inventory activation and review whether excluded configurations apply. Storage administrators can use REST API filters to scan selected blobs, files, containers, file shares, or path prefixes; scans without filters cover the entire storage account. Before enabling the Defender for Endpoint integration, validate connectivity, proxy authentication, file-system settings, security policies, platform and Linux requirements, and install Python 3 on Linux servers. Hunts requires Defender Experts Hunting enrollment and at least the Security Reader role in Microsoft Defender RBAC.

keyChanges.title: Identity inventory moves from opt-in to automatic enablement
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Cloud Apps release notes set October 15, 2026, as the date when Identity inventory integration will automatically enable for eligible tenants that do not use the listed excluded configurations.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Storage supports scoped malware scans
keyChanges.detail: On-demand malware scanning can target individual blobs or files, containers or file shares, or objects matching a path prefix. REST API filters define the scope; without filters, the entire storage account is scanned.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint integration guidance adds prerequisite and sensor details
keyChanges.detail: The Enable Defender For Endpoint guidance now states that the integration can use an existing Defender for Endpoint sensor from the same tenant. It also adds platform and Linux requirements plus checks for connectivity, proxy authentication, file-system settings, and security policies; Linux servers require Python 3.

keyChanges.title: Hunts guidance defines access to expert-led investigations
keyChanges.detail: The new Hunts overview describes how to view in-progress and completed expert-led hunts, including hunt types, statuses, outcomes, and supporting details in the Defender portal. The organization must be enrolled in Defender Experts Hunting, Plan 1, or Plan 2, and the user needs at least the Security Reader role in Microsoft Defender RBAC.

keyChanges.title: Identity sensor v3 activation eligibility is now explicit
keyChanges.detail: The Activate Sensor guidance specifies support for new sensor v3.x deployments on eligible domain controllers without sensor v2.x. It also states that the standalone package activates sensor v3.x on Windows Sense in restricted identity-only mode.

2026-10-06.headline: Defender for Identity details sensor v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint
2026-10-06.overview: The period’s strongest operational changes affect Identity onboarding, Defender for Cloud KSPM scope, and Linux golden-image provisioning. Teams meeting-reporting setup and Sentinel’s ASIM Email Event reference also gained concrete guidance. Most remaining edits are navigation, capitalization, link, and wording maintenance.
2026-10-06.adminImpact: Verify the required operating system and active Microsoft Defender for Identity license before using the sensor activation path. Update Linux image automation and KSPM triage procedures, and review the Teams meeting-reporting control if that workflow is in use. The Sentinel reference supports normalization work; the mechanical documentation edits require no action.

keyChanges.title: Identity activation is limited to new sensor v3.x deployments
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance covers sensor v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint on eligible Windows Server 2019 or later domain controllers. It applies only to new sensor v3.x deployments; automatic sensor activation and automatic Windows auditing require an active license that includes Microsoft Defender for Identity. Verify the operating system and licensing before using the method.

keyChanges.title: KSPM recommendations move from running containers to workload controllers
keyChanges.detail: Starting October 5, 2026, KSPM misconfiguration recommendations align with Kubernetes workload controllers rather than individual running container instances. Teams should look for findings against container deployment controllers when locating and triaging recommendations.

keyChanges.title: Linux golden-image guidance gates Defender startup on final hostnames
keyChanges.detail: The deployment article now directs administrators to embed the tenant-specific onboarding file in the golden image, keep `mdatp` stopped during image creation, and start Defender on clones only after each final hostname is set. It also adds onboarding and health checks; image automation should protect the tenant-specific file and follow this startup sequence.

keyChanges.title: Teams meeting reporting now has an explicit Teams admin center control
keyChanges.detail: The setup path now uses the Teams admin center’s `Allow users to report meetings` policy, while the Defender portal step remains to verify `Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams`. Use both controls when configuring meeting-report handling.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel adds a reference for normalized Email Event data
