keyChanges.detail: The new ASIM reference defines email routing, authentication, delivery-outcome, and threat fields, and documents the `_Im_EmailEvent` parser, custom parser naming, and filtering parameters. It provides a common basis for normalizing and querying email data across mail servers, gateways, and inspection systems.

2026-10-08.headline: Defender for Endpoint and Servers guidance details unified inventory, hunting, and RBAC
2026-10-08.overview: This documentation-heavy period’s most consequential updates describe a combined Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers experience in the Microsoft Defender portal, clarify when disabling Defender for Servers automatically offboards eligible servers, and replace manual support-log analyzer steps with self-contained Live Response workflows. Sentinel normalization guidance also adds a unified process-event parser pattern, while most remaining edits are narrower reference, navigation, or release-entry maintenance.
2026-10-08.adminImpact: Review the server experience requirements before changing configuration. Distinguish disabling Defender for Servers from switching Plan 2 to Plan 1 when assessing offboarding impact. For support collection, select the binary or Python workflow that matches device prerequisites, utilities, and HTTPS access. Update Sentinel parser queries and connector procedures where the revised guidance applies.

keyChanges.title: Unified server experience guidance consolidates endpoint and server workflows
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint page now describes bringing Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers together in the Microsoft Defender portal for Azure and on-premises servers, covering server asset views, investigations, hunting, RBAC, and device groups. It states that existing Defender for Endpoint servers require no onboarding, reinstallation, or migration; administrators should still review capability requirements before changing configuration.

keyChanges.title: Offboarding guidance distinguishes disabling Defender for Servers from a Plan 2-to-Plan 1 switch
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Cloud tutorial states that disabling Defender for Servers for Azure subscriptions in public preview automatically offboards eligible servers, while switching from Plan 2 to Plan 1 does not trigger automatic offboarding. Administrators should account for that distinction when changing coverage.

keyChanges.title: Collect Support Log guidance moves to self-contained binary and Python actions
keyChanges.detail: The updated Endpoint procedure replaces manual analyzer-download steps with self-contained binary or Python Live Response action pairs, adds package validation and workspace-ID handoff, and specifies prerequisites and HTTPS requirements. It also documents a local workflow for devices without Microsoft endpoint access; binary actions do not require Python, while Python actions do.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel normalization guidance adds the unified imProcessEvent parser
keyChanges.detail: The normalization schema page now documents imProcessEvent for querying all process event types while retaining specialized parsers. It also revises custom-parser naming guidance and the filtering example, giving parser owners updated names and query patterns to apply.

keyChanges.title: Azure DevOps connector setup now starts in Agentic code scanning management
keyChanges.detail: The Exposure Management guide directs administrators to Agentic code scanning management, select Add another beside Source code environment, and choose Azure DevOps to open the connector flow. Connector configuration should follow that updated navigation.

2026-10-09.headline: AI agent support matrix clarifies Defender for Endpoint’s activity-based discovery
2026-10-09.overview: The period’s most consequential administrator guidance concerns local AI agents in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. A new support matrix covers supported agents, MCP server discovery, and runtime protection by operating system and configuration, while related pages clarify that discovery depends on observed activity. Sentinel also added specific custom-parser guidance. Most remaining updates—32 in Microsoft Security Exposure Management—were page-attribution maintenance.
2026-10-09.adminImpact: Use the AI agent support matrix to verify documented coverage, and interpret agent inventory as activity-based security context rather than a complete software inventory. An installed agent may not appear until it becomes active. For Sentinel custom parsers, review the generated table’s `disabled=false` setting and forward `pack` only when the source-specific parser supports it. No action is indicated for the attribution-only updates.

keyChanges.title: New matrix separates AI agent support by operating system and configuration
keyChanges.detail: A new Microsoft Defender for Endpoint article documents supported local AI agents, MCP server discovery, and runtime protection scenarios, with support listed separately by operating system and configuration. It also explains that discovery depends on observed agent activity.

keyChanges.title: Installed agents may remain absent until Defender observes activity
keyChanges.detail: The local-agent guidance states that Defender lists an agent after observing activity on an onboarded device; installation alone does not guarantee discovery. It also says the inventory is not a complete software inventory, directing administrators to Software inventory for installed-software details and the support matrix for coverage.

keyChanges.title: Runtime protection guidance broadens inspection-point terminology
keyChanges.detail: The AI Agent Runtime Protection overview now uses broader descriptions of inspection points, streamlines its explanations of agent-native and network inspection, updates discovery terminology, and removes the explicit event-point list and vendor links.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel parser guidance sets disabled=false and conditions pack forwarding
keyChanges.detail: Normalization guidance now explains that the generated table sets `disabled=false` to enable custom parsers and advises forwarding `pack` only when the source-specific parser supports it. Review custom unifying parser functions for these parameter expectations.

keyChanges.title: Exposure Management updates largely change page attribution
keyChanges.detail: A broad Microsoft Security Exposure Management sweep changed author metadata across connector, attack-surface, and vulnerability/exposure pages. For example, the OT data connectors page now credits DebLanger instead of limwainstein/lwainstein. These edits indicate no administrator action.

2026-10-10.headline: SAP BTP application vulnerability findings and Netskope deprecation mark Sentinel reference updates
2026-10-10.overview: Sentinel’s updated connector references add coverage for SAP BTP application vulnerability findings, revise Corelight access requirements, and change the connector catalog by deprecating Netskope Web Transactions, removing older entries, and adding Snowflake V3 tables.
2026-10-10.adminImpact: For the documented SAP BTP connector, enable API access and create dedicated client credentials. Corelight deployments now need Reader and Microsoft Graph access in addition to Monitoring Metrics Publisher. Review integrations, queries, and runbooks that reference deprecated Netskope tables or removed Snowflake V2, Okta, and SentinelOne entries.

keyChanges.title: SAP BTP vulnerability findings connector added to the reference
keyChanges.detail: The Data Connectors Reference now lists a connector that ingests SAP BTP application vulnerability findings into Microsoft Sentinel. Using it requires API access and dedicated client credentials.

keyChanges.title: Corelight access requirements now include Reader and Microsoft Graph
keyChanges.detail: The updated reference lists Reader and Microsoft Graph access as required for Corelight deployments, in addition to Monitoring Metrics Publisher.

keyChanges.title: Netskope Web Transactions is labeled deprecated
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel Tables Connectors Reference now marks the Netskope Web Transactions connector as deprecated and removes the Snowflake V2, Okta, and SentinelOne entries. It also adds new connectors and Snowflake V3 tables.

2026-10-11.headline: File Integrity Monitoring guidance specifies subscription-level Security Admin or Owner roles
2026-10-11.overview: The period brought two Defender for Cloud documentation updates. The most consequential change clarifies that enabling, disabling, or changing File Integrity Monitoring requires Security Admin or Owner on the subscription containing the Log Analytics workspace; Security Reader can view results. Updated release notes also describe a server asset page combining cloud and endpoint details, link to server offboarding guidance, and reference the new Defender server security experience.
2026-10-11.adminImpact: Review role assignments and subscription scope for administrators managing File Integrity Monitoring. Use Security Reader for view-only access to results where appropriate. For server operations, use the updated release-note references to review combined server information and locate offboarding procedures.

keyChanges.title: File Integrity Monitoring access is tied to the Log Analytics workspace subscription
keyChanges.detail: The guidance specifies that Security Admin or Owner roles on the subscription containing the Log Analytics workspace are required to enable, disable, or change File Integrity Monitoring. Security Reader can view the results.

keyChanges.title: Release notes describe combined server details and offboarding guidance
keyChanges.detail: Updated Defender for Cloud release notes describe a server asset page combining cloud and endpoint details, link to server offboarding guidance, and reference the new Defender server security experience.

2026-10-12.headline: Mobile TVM guidance warns restrictive Conditional Access can disrupt service flows
2026-10-12.overview: Updates center on Mobile TVM connectivity and Conditional Access, with additional Endpoint tagging limitations and a Defender for Identity role-table change.
2026-10-12.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies affecting Mobile TVM, allow the documented Android and iOS Defender for Endpoint domains through applicable firewalls and proxies, and avoid treating the DeviceTagging Group registry value as a complete tag inventory. Identity administrators should also account for the Security Operator role when reviewing Revoke session permissions.

keyChanges.title: Mobile TVM guidance identifies Conditional Access disruption risks
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance lists onboarding, security reporting, and iOS TVM as Mobile TVM service uses. It warns that restrictive Conditional Access policies can disrupt these flows and recommends excluding the service from those policies.

keyChanges.title: Android and iOS onboarding guidance adds cross-cloud network requirements
keyChanges.detail: The Mtd article now lists the firewall and proxy URLs required to onboard and maintain Microsoft Defender for Endpoint devices on Android and iOS in both commercial and US Government cloud environments. Administrators should verify that the applicable domains are allowed.

keyChanges.title: DeviceTagging registry guidance limits Group values to one tag
keyChanges.detail: The DeviceTagging registry key supports only one tag in the Group value. Tags assigned through other methods are not written there, so the registry value may not represent every tag on a device; multiple tags should use another supported tagging method.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity lists Security Operator for Revoke session
keyChanges.detail: The remediation-actions table now includes Security Operator among the roles for the Revoke session action, giving administrators an additional role to consider when reviewing or assigning session-revocation permissions.

2026-10-13.headline: Defender XDR guidance details explicit per-rule controls for custom detections
2026-10-13.overview: The period is dominated by documentation maintenance, but four updates carry useful operational detail. Defender XDR guidance now clearly describes default correlation, per-rule exclusions, and single-alert behavior for custom detections. Separate guidance covers July 2026 bulk-mail routing, Azure CSPM prerequisites for recommendation exemptions, and Defender for Containers provisioning failures.
2026-10-13.adminImpact: Use the per-rule correlation control when managing custom detections; there is no tenant-level custom-detection setting. Assign the Azure CSPM standard when exemptions are needed, use the new Defender for Containers diagnostics for affected EKS or Arc environments, and review anti-spam expectations for promotional bulk mail.

keyChanges.title: Custom detections have documented per-rule correlation controls
keyChanges.detail: The updated Defender XDR guidance states that custom detections are included in correlation by default and can be included or excluded on a per-rule basis. When a rule is excluded and no matching grouping rule applies, it produces a predictable single-alert incident. The page also states that no tenant-level custom-detection setting is available.

keyChanges.title: Promotional bulk-mail routing is spelled out for July 2026
keyChanges.detail: The Office 365 anti-spam guidance says that, as of July 2026, messages identified as bulk receive the Promotions tag. When Bulk moves enabled is turned on, messages move from Inbox to the Promotions folder only when they are promotional in nature, regardless of BCL value.

keyChanges.title: Azure CSPM assignment controls exemptions for some recommendations
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Cloud guidance now explains that some identity and access recommendations can appear without the Azure CSPM standard assigned, but those recommendations do not support exemptions unless the standard is assigned. Administrators needing exemptions should assign the standard and follow the linked assignment procedure.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Containers adds EKS and Azure Arc troubleshooting paths
keyChanges.detail: The troubleshooting guidance now covers EKS provisioning failures caused by recreated IAM roles, endpoint allowlist reconciliation, and stale Azure Arc registrations. It adds diagnostic commands and resolution steps, including preserving required Defender provisioning network ranges in infrastructure automation.

2026-10-14.headline: Defender for Identity sensor v3 guidance shifts to September cumulative updates
2026-10-14.overview: This was primarily a documentation-maintenance day—22 updates and one removed page, with no new entries—but several changes have direct operational consequences. Defender for Identity guidance now centers on September 2026 Windows Server updates and clarifies sensor migration and offboarding behavior. Defender for Cloud documents an AWS scan-suspension threshold, while Defender XDR clarifies both the AIAgentsInfo-to-AgentsInfo schema transition and where DLP signals can be investigated.
2026-10-14.adminImpact: Install the September 2026 cumulative update before deploying or upgrading eligible Defender for Identity sensor v3 systems, select the local system account option before v2 migration, and handle leftover workspace DSA or gMSA configuration separately after verifying usage. Do not expect offboarding Defender for Endpoint to enable identity-only operation; use the documented onboarding method that excludes Defender for Endpoint. For AWS agentless scanning, verify ec2:DeleteSnapshot authorization and monitor cleanup because 250 or more undeletable Defender-tagged snapshots suspend new scans in the affected scope. Use AgentsInfo for agent-related hunting and advanced hunting for the documented DLP signals.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity sensor v3 prerequisites move to September 2026 cumulative updates
keyChanges.detail: The Deploy Sensor V3 guidance replaces the July 2026 prerequisite with the September 2026 Windows Server cumulative update for sensor version 3.0.10 or later. It also clarifies that administrators should select the local system account option before v2 migration and that migration does not automatically remove workspace DSA or gMSA configuration.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity guidance separates Endpoint offboarding from identity-only operation
keyChanges.detail: The FAQ states that offboarding a server from Defender for Endpoint stops Defender for Identity v3.x sensor reporting, including sensors migrated from v2.x, and does not automatically enable identity-only mode. Deployments needing identity-only protection should use the onboarding method that excludes Defender for Endpoint.

keyChanges.title: AWS agentless scanning suspends new scans after 250 failed-deletion snapshots
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Cloud guidance says that 250 or more Defender-tagged snapshots accumulated because of deletion authorization failures suspend new scans for the affected AWS scope. The snapshots continue accruing storage charges until deleted, so administrators should verify ec2:DeleteSnapshot authorization and review AWS policy restrictions.

keyChanges.title: Advanced hunting transitions agent data from AIAgentsInfo to AgentsInfo
keyChanges.detail: The AIAgentsInfo reference was removed as the schema transitions to unified AgentsInfo, which expands beyond Copilot Studio-specific columns. The removed reference states that AIAgentsInfo remains accessible until July 1, 2026; affected queries should be updated to AgentsInfo.

keyChanges.title: DLP signals remain in advanced hunting rather than the incident queue
keyChanges.detail: The guidance says the built-in rule took effect in early October 2026, but DLP signals are treated as behaviors: they do not generate alerts or appear in the incident queue and remain available in advanced hunting. Investigators should use advanced hunting for these signals.

2026-10-15.headline: App Governance retires two EWS-based detections effective October 15
2026-10-15.overview: The period's most consequential change is an App Governance retirement: two EWS-based detections are now retired and no longer generate alerts. Other substantive updates refine the documented scope of Microsoft Store vulnerability assessment, add Defender for Identity GPO risk-assessment guidance, expand the Cloud Apps migration support list, and announce localized default Mark and notify messages in Defender for Office 365.
2026-10-15.adminImpact: Administrators should no longer rely on the two retired detections for alerting, use the limited Store-app coverage and revised migration matrix for planning, and review the new GPO assessment guidance before changing affected policies. The localized Mark and notify template requires no action and does not change message classification or custom templates.

keyChanges.title: Two EWS-based App Governance detections are now retired
keyChanges.detail: As of October 15, 2026, two EWS-based detections are marked Retired and no longer generate alerts. Cloud Apps administrators should not rely on them for detection coverage after that date.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity guidance adds two GPO assessment scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance now covers excessive local-group privileges granted by Group Policy Objects and reversible passwords stored in Group Policy Preferences. It includes the associated risks, user impact, remediation steps, and dependencies to check before making changes.

keyChanges.title: TVM now describes limited Store-app vulnerability coverage
keyChanges.detail: The Software Inventory page no longer labels Microsoft Store applications as Preview or lists individual supported apps. It now states that vulnerability assessment is available for a limited set of commonly used Microsoft Store applications.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Apps migration guidance adds auto-labeling and four DLP sources
keyChanges.detail: The guide now lists auto-labeling migration for SharePoint and OneDrive, plus DLP file-policy migration for Google Workspace, Box, Dropbox, and Salesforce. The previous list contained only SharePoint and OneDrive DLP migration, so administrators should use the revised support list when planning migrations.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Office 365 will localize the default notification template
keyChanges.detail: The default “Mark and notify” email template will be localized according to each user's Outlook language settings, with global rollout starting in June 2026. Message classification and custom templates remain unchanged, and no administrator action is required.

2026-10-16.headline: Endpoint release notes add Platform 4.18.26090.9 and ASR path-handling details
2026-10-16.overview: The most consequential update adds Endpoint platform, engine, and security intelligence release details alongside protection-engine, update-reliability, ASR, and policy-exclusion notes. Defender for Cloud also materially changes a SQL Server coverage query, while Defender XDR updates expand AI-agent blocking guidance and remove preview labels from several custom-role headings.
2026-10-16.adminImpact: Endpoint administrators should review automation using the renamed ConfigurationProtection PowerShell property and validate deployments against the documented protection and ASR behavior. Teams reusing the SQL Server query should review saved copies because its filters and output fields changed. AI-agent administrators can use the expanded guidance to identify where blocking rules affect interactions; the RBAC heading changes require no action.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint release documentation adds platform, engine, and intelligence versions
keyChanges.detail: The page now lists Platform 4.18.26090.9, Engine 1.1.26090.9, and security intelligence 1.461.1.0. It also documents automatic protection-engine refresh, improved update reliability, ASR path handling, policy-exclusion retention, and the renamed PowerShell property ConfigurationProtection.

keyChanges.title: SQL Server coverage KQL now filters through Log Analytics workspaces
keyChanges.detail: The example now queries SQL Vulnerability Assessment records, filters resources by Log Analytics workspace IDs, and returns workspace ID, machine name, and machine UUID. The previous subassessment, OnPremiseSql, and 30-day scan-time filters were removed, so saved queries should be reviewed.

keyChanges.title: AI-agent protection guidance maps blocks across requests and responses
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now covers malicious content propagation, secret exfiltration, evasion techniques, and unsafe email domains. It explains how enabled blocking rules affect user requests, model responses, tool requests, and tool responses.

keyChanges.title: Custom RBAC role headings remove preview labels
keyChanges.detail: The MTO URBAC page no longer includes “(Preview)” in headings for creating or editing custom roles, deleting roles, and importing roles. Reference links were also updated.

2026-10-17.headline: Sentinel connector references add SilentPush and Theom, remove Red Canary listings
2026-10-17.overview: Sentinel reference updates add SilentPush Feeds and Theom coverage while removing Red Canary entries. The Office 365 anti-spam page also moves its stated availability expectation for features, including SOC experiences, from mid-September to the end of October.
2026-10-17.adminImpact: Review the revised Sentinel connector references when deploying or troubleshooting integrations. CrowdStrike administrators should verify the listed REST API scopes and use the updated parser for existing queries; affected connector deployments should follow the revised vendor guidance. Office 365 administrators should adjust rollout expectations; no specific action is stated.

keyChanges.title: Data Connectors Reference revises CrowdStrike, Pathlock, and SilentPush guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel reference now lists required CrowdStrike REST API scopes, links to upgrade notes, adds Pathlock deployment guidance, removes the Red Canary connector section, and adds SilentPush Feeds details. CrowdStrike administrators should verify the listed scopes and use the updated parser for existing queries.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel Tables reference adds three connector entries and removes one
keyChanges.detail: The table adds SilentPush Feeds, Theom, and Theom via the Codeless Connector Framework, while removing the Red Canary Threat Detection entry. Administrators using the reference should consult the revised table for current connector listings and table names.

keyChanges.title: Office 365 anti-spam availability expectation moves to end of October
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now says the features, including SOC experiences, should be available in all organizations by the end of October rather than mid-September. No administrator action is stated beyond updating rollout expectations.

2026-10-19.headline: Defender for Identity sets a 30-day opt-out before sensor v3.x defaults activate
2026-10-19.overview: Eligible organizations with an active Defender for Identity workspace receive a banner 30 days before sensor v3.x activation and Windows auditing are enabled by default, including settings currently set to Off. Related guidance separates v2.x and v3.x deployment, migration, connectivity, and account procedures. Defender XDR guidance specifies per-detection-source alert tuning and updates CloudDnsEvents field names. Android guidance clarifies the onboarding and policy sequence, while Message Center item MC1478465 says to disregard its Security Copilot E5/E7 notice because it reached the wrong audience.
2026-10-19.adminImpact: Identity administrators should use the banner's Opt out control within 30 days if they need to retain current settings, verify that “Automatically use the sensor's local system account” is selected before sensor v3 migration, and confirm that in-place migration targets an eligible domain controller. Update CloudDnsEvents queries to use EventType and EventSubType. Android administrators should onboard devices, approve and sync the Defender app through Managed Google Play, and then create the app configuration policy. MC1478465 requires no action other than disregarding the message.

keyChanges.title: Sensor v3.x activation and Windows auditing get a 30-day opt-out window
keyChanges.detail: For eligible organizations with an active Defender for Identity workspace, the banner appears 30 days before sensor v3.x activation and Windows auditing are enabled by default, including settings currently set to Off. Selecting Opt out preserves the current settings. The update also records Windows Server 2025 sensor migration support as resolved.

keyChanges.title: Sensor v3 migration does not change the action-account setting
keyChanges.detail: Before migrating, administrators must select and verify “Automatically use the sensor's local system account.” The migration does not change this setting automatically, and leaving gMSA selected can affect response actions.

keyChanges.title: In-place v2.x-to-v3.x migration is limited to eligible domain controllers
keyChanges.detail: The deployment guidance states that in-place migration is currently available only for eligible domain controllers, not other servers, and links to the v2.x requirements and migration prerequisites. Check server roles before planning migration.

keyChanges.title: Defender XDR alert-tuning guidance specifies per-detection-source selection
keyChanges.detail: When creating or editing alert-tuning rules, administrators can select individual detection sources within service sources, including include or exclude choices for existing rules. This enables more precise tuning without requiring a stated configuration change.

keyChanges.title: CloudDnsEvents hunting fields now use EventType and EventSubType
keyChanges.detail: The table reference replaces DnsEventType and DnsEventSubType with EventType and EventSubType and updates the request-filter example. Existing CloudDnsEvents queries should use the revised column names.

2026-10-20.headline: Defender portal preview brings Azure plan management, DWU billing, and server onboarding
2026-10-20.overview: Defender for Cloud is the clear center of gravity: new and revised guidance describes a preview for connecting Azure commercial subscriptions or management groups, managing cloud security plans in the Defender portal, and estimating costs with Defender Workload Units (DWUs). Migration changes configuration scope, makes migrated Azure portal settings view-only, and does not preserve resource-level configurations. Supporting updates clarify tenant-wide server onboarding, broaden Defender for Identity sensor v3.x coverage, and flag an upcoming Defender for Cloud Apps permission change.
2026-10-20.adminImpact: Before adopting Defender portal plan management, verify Azure commercial eligibility and required permissions, model DWU costs, and inventory resource-level settings because migration does not preserve them. Treat Direct onboarding as tenant-wide rather than a pilot switch, and confirm the documented telemetry, tenant, and role prerequisites. Review affected App Governance role assignments before permission changes begin in mid-November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud plan management moves into a scoped portal preview
keyChanges.detail: New preview guidance covers connecting Azure subscriptions or management groups and configuring plans globally or at tenant, management-group, or subscription scope. After migration, plan settings become view-only in the Azure portal, and resource-level configurations are not preserved.

keyChanges.title: DWU guidance adds cost estimation and post-adoption reporting
keyChanges.detail: New guidance introduces Defender Workload Units, a Cloud Security Cost Estimator, and a Cloud security cost report. It also documents updated workload measurements, plan consolidations, and DNS billing treatment under the new model.

keyChanges.title: Direct onboarding is explicitly tenant-wide for eligible non-Azure servers
keyChanges.detail: The updated procedure states that Direct onboarding affects all eligible existing and future non-Azure servers in the same Microsoft Entra tenant; individual-server or pilot-group selection is unsupported. Administrators must verify healthy Defender for Endpoint telemetry, a matching tenant, and the required roles before enabling it.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity sensor v3.x expands to more Windows Server roles
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance documents sensor v3.x onboarding with or without Defender for Endpoint for eligible Windows Server 2019 or later AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers, extending the documented coverage beyond domain controllers.

keyChanges.title: App Governance permissions will change for three Entra roles
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps will align App Governance role-based access with Defender XDR. The change affects the Cloud App Security, Compliance Administrator, and Compliance Data Administrator roles, so administrators should review and update role assignments.

2026-10-21.headline: Sentinel details a preview SAP BTP vulnerability connector and vulnerable-app detection
2026-10-21.overview: The substantive change this period is a Sentinel SAP BTP solution expansion in preview: guidance now covers Application Vulnerability Report Service findings, companion analytics, and workbook content. Defender XDR also records a time-limited Advanced Hunting schema transition, while Defender for Endpoint updates macOS release guidance and clarifies offboarding behavior. Other edits mainly correct access instructions, links, naming, metadata, and notification-language references.
2026-10-21.adminImpact: Update queries using `AadDeviceId` to `EntraIdDeviceId` within the stated 30-day overlap. For SAP BTP, the connector setup has documented prerequisites, credentials, polling, and ingestion-delay settings; the correlation rule requires both SAP BTP AVL and audit-event connectors. Review Defender URBAC role and data-plane permissions before granting delegated remote-tenant Sentinel access. For endpoint operations, review the macOS EDR runtime-protection support and remember that offboarding eligible Azure servers and uninstalling Defender software are separate actions.

keyChanges.title: SAP BTP solution guidance documents a preview vulnerability-finding connector
keyChanges.detail: The solution overview now separates SAP BTP Application Vulnerability Report Service findings into a preview connector and adds a preview analytics rule plus an Application Vulnerabilities workbook tab with a vulnerability-posture KPI. The documented use case is to combine these findings with BTP audit activity when investigating vulnerable custom applications.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting begins a 30-day `AadDeviceId` to `EntraIdDeviceId` transition
keyChanges.detail: The schema-change notice says `AadDeviceId` is being replaced by `EntraIdDeviceId`; the old column remains available for 30 days so administrators can update hunting queries.

keyChanges.title: Defender URBAC guidance adds delegated remote-tenant Sentinel access steps
keyChanges.detail: The updated procedure covers required permissions, role assignment, and workspace selection for delegated remote tenant groups, while retaining resource-group assignment as an option. It also separates management-plane permissions from any additional data-plane access required.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint offboarding guidance separates automatic Azure and manual server paths
keyChanges.detail: The updated page covers Windows, Linux client and server, macOS, Android, and iOS. It distinguishes subscription-wide Azure server offboarding when Defender for Servers is turned off from manual individual-server offboarding, and states that offboarding does not uninstall the software.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint macOS release adds EDR configuration for AI agent runtime protection
keyChanges.detail: Release 101.26082.0012 is documented with EDR support for configuring AI agent runtime protection, alongside Bluetooth permission and antivirus-health reporting improvements plus accessibility, reliability, and performance fixes.

2026-10-22.headline: Defender XDR adds URL-click alerts to permission guidance and revises actor mappings
2026-10-22.overview: Two Defender XDR reference pages changed. Custom Permissions Details now includes URL-click alerts in the alert types supported by the “Emails associated with alerts” read permission, alongside malware/phish and junk reports. Microsoft Threat Actor Naming now associates Sunglow Blizzard with Russia and removes Storm-0156 and Storm-1849 from its table.
2026-10-22.adminImpact: Administrators reviewing custom permission scope should account for the expanded alert-type list, while threat-intelligence and security teams should use the revised naming table when interpreting Microsoft threat actor references.

keyChanges.title: URL-click alerts added to custom permission scope guidance
keyChanges.detail: The “Emails associated with alerts” read permission now lists URL-click alerts alongside malware/phish and junk reports. Use the expanded list when reviewing custom permission scope and email-content access.

keyChanges.title: Threat actor naming table revises group associations
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Threat Actor Naming table now lists Sunglow Blizzard as associated with Russia and removes the Storm-0156 and Storm-1849 entries. The page date is October 21, 2026.

2026-10-23.headline: Defender documents Android SilentRunMode and Mac Promotions-folder bulk-mail behavior
2026-10-23.overview: Two targeted Microsoft Learn updates shaped the period. Endpoint release notes document Silent running mode for Shared Device Management on Android: administrators set SilentRunMode to 1 to enable it, or 0—the default—to disable it. The anti-spam behavior matrix adds Outlook for Mac, stating that bulk mail below the BCL threshold can be delivered to Promotions and that permanently deleting the folder causes it to be recreated within a few minutes.
2026-10-23.adminImpact: Administrators managing shared Android devices can configure SilentRunMode, but no required action is stated. Teams supporting Outlook for Mac should account for the Promotions-folder behavior when troubleshooting bulk-mail delivery; no administrator action is stated.

keyChanges.title: SilentRunMode documented for shared Android device management
keyChanges.detail: The October 2026 Android release notes specify Silent running mode for Shared Device Management. Set SilentRunMode to 1 to enable the mode or 0 to disable it; 0 is the default.

keyChanges.title: Outlook for Mac bulk-mail behavior added to the anti-spam matrix
keyChanges.detail: The matrix now indicates that bulk mail below the BCL threshold can be delivered to Outlook for Mac's Promotions folder. If the folder is permanently deleted, it is recreated within a few minutes.

2026-10-24.headline: Sentinel connector troubleshooting adds role guidance while Endpoint redirects EOSDate remediation
2026-10-24.overview: Sentinel's Azure Storage Blob connector troubleshooting now specifies service-principal role assignments and Event Grid permission handling. Endpoint's Windows MMA agent guidance no longer recommends the EOSDate column in Advanced Hunting, directing administrators instead to end-of-support software guidance and Defender for Endpoint vulnerability management.
2026-10-24.adminImpact: Administrators troubleshooting Sentinel connector authorization failures can follow the documented Storage Blob Data Reader and Storage Queue Data Contributor assignments, including the Event Grid storage queue guidance. Teams managing outdated Windows agents should use the updated remediation paths to help avoid service disruption.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel documents the roles required for Azure Storage Blob connector authorization
keyChanges.detail: The troubleshooting article now explains how to assign Storage Blob Data Reader and Storage Queue Data Contributor to the Sentinel service principal, and adds guidance for Event Grid storage queue permission errors.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint replaces EOSDate hunting guidance with remediation references
keyChanges.detail: The Windows MMA agent article no longer recommends using the EOSDate column in Advanced Hunting. It now directs administrators to end-of-support software guidance and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint vulnerability management to track remediation.

2026-10-25.headline: Defender for Identity clarifies Windows Server 2016 sensor behavior after extended support ends
2026-10-25.overview: The four updates tightened lifecycle, deployment, and navigation guidance. Defender for Identity documentation says sensors continue reporting and receiving updates after Windows Server 2016 extended support ends, although some functionality may be affected. Defender for Containers guidance states that its sensor does not support GKE Autopilot clusters. Identity health guidance also flags Windows Server 2016 as approaching extended end of support while Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 remain unsupported.
2026-10-25.adminImpact: Plan Windows Server 2016 sensor upgrades with the documented post-support limitations in mind, and use Legacy operating systems guidance to assess sensors on systems nearing or past support. Exclude GKE Autopilot clusters from Defender for Containers sensor deployment plans. For cloud security cost reporting, use the updated Defender portal path: Setup & configuration > Costs & usage.

keyChanges.title: Server 2016 sensor lifecycle guidance
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisites page says sensors continue reporting to Defender for Identity and receiving updates after Windows Server 2016 extended support ends, although some functionality may be affected.

keyChanges.title: GKE Autopilot sensor support limitation
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Containers deployment guidance now states that the sensor does not support GKE Autopilot clusters.

keyChanges.title: Health guidance distinguishes approaching and unsupported Windows versions
keyChanges.detail: The health-alert guidance identifies Windows Server 2016 as approaching extended end of support and links to Legacy operating systems guidance; Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 remain identified as unsupported.

keyChanges.title: Updated path for cloud cost reporting
keyChanges.detail: The portal comparison now lists the Defender portal location for cloud security cost reporting as Setup & configuration > Costs & usage.

2026-10-26.headline: Advanced Hunting API retirement sets January 2027 migration deadline
2026-10-26.overview: Microsoft will retire the Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs by February 1, 2027; workflows must be manually migrated to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31. The period also brings a rolling Teams message-content table, an Endpoint Linux release with Azure Linux 4 support and socket-bind telemetry, and clearer AKS policy guidance for Defender for Cloud Security Gating.
2026-10-26.adminImpact: Inventory integrations that use the retiring hunting APIs and schedule manual migration before January 31, 2027. During the MessageContents rollout, verify that analysts have the required permissions. Before enabling Security Gating, check AKS Deny policy assignments and coordinate any Audit-mode change or narrowly scoped exemption with the Azure Policy administrator. Plan Azure Linux 4 coverage and use the new telemetry once it reaches the tenant; use the revised Sentinel residency wording for data-handling assessments.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting APIs retire on February 1, 2027
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs are scheduled for retirement by February 1, 2027. Existing workflows must be manually migrated to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027.

keyChanges.title: Teams message snippets and metadata enter Advanced Hunting
keyChanges.detail: The new MessageContents table is rolling out in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Advanced Hunting from late September through mid-November 2026. Authorized analysts can query Teams message snippets and metadata for investigations, subject to specific permissions.

keyChanges.title: AKS Deny policies can block Security Gating provisioning
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Cloud guidance now documents that Deny policies targeting AKS managed clusters can produce RequestDisallowedByPolicy during Security Gating provisioning, even for compliant clusters. Administrators can identify the blocking assignment in the Activity Log and coordinate an Audit-mode change or narrowly scoped exemption.

keyChanges.title: October Linux release adds Azure Linux 4 and socket-bind telemetry
keyChanges.detail: The October 2026 Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Linux release notes list version 101.26091.0004, Azure Linux 4 support, and TCP socket bind telemetry. After gradual rollout, the telemetry will be available in Advanced Hunting through DeviceNetworkEvents.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel residency guidance revises regional data handling
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel residency page now states that processed and configuration data are processed and stored in onboarding destination regions or applicable existing Defender XDR regions. It adds processed-data examples and removes the 21Vianet retirement notice.

2026-10-27.headline: MDASH guidance names MAI-Cyber-1.1-Flash and flags Device Control v1 retirement
2026-10-27.overview: Exposure Management updates identify MAI Cyber (Preview) as the recommended MDASH scan configuration and replace MAI-Cyber-1-Flash with MAI-Cyber-1.1-Flash. The updated guidance says existing Foundry configurations are upgraded automatically. Separately, Endpoint release notes for macOS version 101.26092.0009 document improved policy reliability, antivirus performance and health reporting, EDR updates, and Legacy Device Control v1 retirement. Defender XDR also received a structural and link refresh.
2026-10-27.adminImpact: Administrators configuring MDASH should use the updated model name. Standard remains the default scan configuration, while MAI Cyber can be selected during onboarding or changed later; existing Foundry configurations are described as upgrading automatically, with no required action stated. Endpoint administrators should account for Device Control v1 retirement. The new health reporting can help verify Bluetooth permissions and Microsoft Defender system-extension configuration.

keyChanges.title: MAI Cyber guidance adopts the newer scan model
keyChanges.detail: The updated What's New entry says MAI Cyber (Preview) now uses MAI-Cyber-1.1-Flash instead of MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, identifies MAI Cyber as the recommended MDASH scan configuration, and says existing Foundry configurations are upgraded automatically.

keyChanges.title: Onboarding guidance keeps Standard as the default
keyChanges.detail: The Ai Code Security Onboarding guidance states that Standard remains the default MDASH scan configuration. It recommends MAI Cyber (Preview), which can be selected during onboarding or changed later.

keyChanges.title: macOS release notes document Legacy Device Control v1 retirement
keyChanges.detail: The notes for macOS version 101.26092.0009 cover improved policy reliability, antivirus performance and health reporting, EDR updates, and retirement of Legacy Device Control v1. The health reporting helps verify Bluetooth permissions and Microsoft Defender system-extension configuration.

keyChanges.title: Defender XDR threat guidance receives structural cleanup
keyChanges.detail: The page now has a new security-imperative heading, revised introductory text, streamlined job-to-be-done formatting, two fewer ontology links, and an updated date. This is a page-organization and link change; no required administrator action is stated.

2026-10-28.headline: Defender for Identity guidance flags v3 government-cloud prerequisites and v2 sensor limits
2026-10-28.overview: Defender for Identity guidance now documents two deployment constraints: v3.x sensor activation without Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is temporarily unsupported in government clouds, while v2.x sensor installation in new workspaces created from October 2026 is restricted in preview. The period also adds the CloudKeyVaultEvents advanced-hunting table for Azure Key Vault activity, revises Sentinel connector status references, and expands Defender XDR role-permission guidance.
2026-10-28.adminImpact: Review identity sensor deployment plans for new workspaces: eligible Windows Server 2019 or later domain controllers are directed to the v3.x deployment guidance and onboarding package, while government-cloud v3.x activation requires Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Hunting teams can use CloudKeyVaultEvents when Microsoft Defender for Cloud is available. Sentinel administrators should validate connector inventories and status references, and RBAC owners can reassess coverage for core cloud security settings.

keyChanges.title: Government-cloud v3.x sensor activation now carries a Defender for Endpoint prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Identity What's New guidance states that activating the v3.x sensor without Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is temporarily unsupported in government cloud environments.

keyChanges.title: New workspaces are directed to v3.x onboarding for eligible domain controllers
keyChanges.detail: Install Sensor guidance marks the v2.x sensor restriction for new workspaces as preview. For workspaces created from October 2026, eligible Windows Server 2019 or later domain controllers are directed to the v3.x deployment guidance and onboarding package.

keyChanges.title: CloudKeyVaultEvents adds Azure Key Vault activity to advanced hunting
keyChanges.detail: The new Defender XDR table documents Azure Key Vault operations, access identities, request details, and operation results, with schema fields and sample queries. Queries require Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel reference now labels Jira Audit and SecurityScorecard Factor deprecated
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel Tables Connectors Reference marks the Atlassian Jira Audit and SecurityScorecard Factor connectors as deprecated. It also updates connector names and links, removes GoogleCloudSCC, adds entries, and changes availability indicators for multiple connectors.

keyChanges.title: Defender XDR RBAC guidance adds core cloud-security management permissions
keyChanges.detail: The role comparison page now lists Management permissions for reading or managing environment connections, plan enablement, and policy configuration.

2026-10-29.headline: Exposure Management guidance defines exemptions while Defender clarifies suspended-scan charges
2026-10-29.overview: This was a documentation-led period centered on Exposure Management governance and Defender for Cloud cost implications. New guidance covers recommendation exemptions and posture-policy prerequisites, while updated agentless-scanning guidance states that Defender and snapshot charges continue during suspension. Defender XDR also documents the preview CloudKeyVaultEvents hunting table, and Safe Links now names Outlook mobile clients in its API-based URL-check coverage.
2026-10-29.adminImpact: No deadline or mandatory migration is stated. Administrators configuring Exposure Management should verify environment, plan, and RBAC prerequisites. Teams suspending agentless VM scans should budget for continuing Defender charges and snapshot storage until snapshots are deleted. Hunting teams can review CloudKeyVaultEvents for Azure Key Vault activity, and Safe Links owners should include Outlook for iOS and Android when assessing the documented behavior of unwrapped URLs.

keyChanges.title: Recommendation exemptions gain lifecycle and governance guidance
keyChanges.detail: A new Exposure Management page explains how to create and manage recommendation exemptions, including scope, permissions, lifecycle, governance, limitations, and alternatives for devices, SaaS apps, identities, and data. It also helps administrators choose between removing a policy rule and creating an exemption.

keyChanges.title: Posture-policy prerequisites are documented for Exposure Management
keyChanges.detail: The new posture-policy guidance defines cloud-resource scope and lists Defender environment requirements, eligible-plan prerequisites, and RBAC permissions for creating or managing policies.

keyChanges.title: Suspended agentless VM scans still incur Defender and snapshot charges
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Cloud guidance states that charges continue while agentless VM scans are suspended. Existing snapshots continue to incur storage charges until deleted, and the 250-snapshot safeguard is not a guarantee.

keyChanges.title: CloudKeyVaultEvents appears in Advanced Hunting as a preview table
keyChanges.detail: The Advanced Hunting schema now lists CloudKeyVaultEvents, marked Preview, for operations performed against Azure Key Vault resources. Hunting teams can use the documented table when investigating Key Vault activity.

keyChanges.title: Safe Links documents Outlook mobile coverage for unwrapped URLs
keyChanges.detail: Safe Links documentation now includes Outlook for iOS and Android among the clients where API-based URL checks apply when URL wrapping is disabled. Administrators reviewing this setting should include both mobile clients in the documented coverage.

2026-10-30.headline: Azure posture policies and exemptions preview as Teams call hunting arrives
2026-10-30.overview: The day’s meaningful changes are concentrated in two product developments: public-preview posture controls for Azure environments and a November 2026 Defender XDR capability for investigating suspicious Teams calls and meetings. Sentinel guidance also gained targeted SAP ingestion-health queries. With 1,248 updates and no new or removed pages, the remaining supplied changes are predominantly metadata and reference-link maintenance.
2026-10-30.adminImpact: Exposure Management and Defender for Cloud administrators can evaluate Azure resources against the Defender for Cloud baseline, create custom posture policies, and manage accepted-risk exemptions with lifecycle tracking. Teams using Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 can prepare advanced-hunting workflows around CallActivityEvents when worldwide availability begins in November 2026, with connections to the event streaming API and Microsoft Sentinel. Sentinel administrators monitoring SAP collection can use the linked KQL queries to investigate incomplete windows, truncation, volume trends, hourly peaks, and high-volume accounts. The many ontology and authoring-link updates do not indicate configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Azure posture policies and recommendation exemptions enter public preview
keyChanges.detail: Exposure Management guidance says administrators can evaluate Azure resources against the Microsoft Defender for Cloud baseline, create custom posture policies, and centrally manage accepted-risk exemptions with lifecycle tracking. The controls are available in public preview for Azure environments.

keyChanges.title: CallActivityEvents brings Teams call and meeting investigation to Defender XDR
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender XDR will provide the CallActivityEvents table for Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 teams to investigate suspicious Microsoft Teams calls and meetings, including activities, initiators, organizers, and related messages. The capability is scheduled for worldwide availability from November 2026 and integrates with advanced hunting, the event streaming API, and Microsoft Sentinel.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel SAP health guidance adds targeted ingestion-analysis queries
keyChanges.detail: The SAP system health article now links to KQL queries for detecting incomplete collection windows and truncation markers, and for analyzing daily and projected monthly volume, hourly peaks, and high-volume accounts. These queries support investigation of ingestion completeness and volume patterns.

2026-10-31.headline: Promotions folder guidance now names the first promotional message as its trigger
2026-10-31.overview: The period contained one Office 365 email-and-collaboration documentation update. Anti-spam guidance now says a mailbox’s Promotions folder is created when the first promotional message is delivered, rather than the first bulk message.
2026-10-31.adminImpact: No administrator action is required; the update clarifies which message delivery triggers folder creation.

keyChanges.title: Anti-spam guidance changes the folder-creation wording
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now identifies delivery of the first promotional message—not the first bulk message—as the event that creates the mailbox’s Promotions folder.

2026-11-01.headline: AMPLS query restrictions and Storage V2 prerequisites sharpen Sentinel hunting guidance
2026-11-01.overview: Two updated pages deliver concrete administrator guidance: private-endpoint restrictions can block Sentinel data queries through Defender experiences, while the CloudStorageAggregatedEvents table requires subscription-level Defender for Storage V2.
2026-11-01.adminImpact: Administrators using Azure Monitor Private Link Scope should preserve the required Log Analytics query access for Defender portal experiences, Defender APIs, and Advanced Hunting. Teams relying on CloudStorageAggregatedEvents must enable Defender for Storage V2 at the subscription level; storage-account-level enablement and the legacy plan will not populate the table.

keyChanges.title: AMPLS private endpoints limit Defender query access
keyChanges.detail: Azure Monitor Private Link Scope supports Sentinel data ingestion into Log Analytics, but it does not support querying through Defender portal experiences or Defender APIs when query access is restricted to private endpoints. Disabling public Log Analytics query access also makes the data unavailable to experiences such as Advanced Hunting.

keyChanges.title: CloudStorageAggregatedEvents requires subscription-level Storage V2
keyChanges.detail: The table is populated only when Defender for Storage V2 is enabled at the subscription level. Storage-account-level enablement and the legacy plan are not supported for populating the table.

2026-11-02.headline: Defender for Cloud guidance spells out staged and full portal management transfers
2026-11-02.overview: The period was quiet and mostly editorial. The substantive update is more specific Defender for Cloud transfer guidance: it identifies DWU for moving plan enablement and billing to the Defender portal, an optional Management selection for all supported cloud security capabilities, and Managed in status values for verification. The Endpoint updates refresh attribution and remove prerelease wording, while Defender XDR removes a sample RBAC table.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: For cloud-plan transfers, administrators can choose staged or full management and use Managed in to confirm the resulting configuration. The Endpoint edits require no action. Administrators who relied on the removed RBAC sample table should use the revised page.

keyChanges.title: DWU and Management choices are now explicit in plan-transfer guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Cloud page now says to select DWU to move plan enablement and billing to the Defender portal. An optional Management selection moves all supported cloud security capabilities, and Managed in status values show where each environment is managed.

keyChanges.title: Custom data collection article drops its prerelease notice
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint custom data collection article now has updated author and Microsoft author metadata, and its prerelease product notice has been removed.

keyChanges.title: Defender XDR RBAC page removes its sample table
keyChanges.detail: The Manage RBAC page no longer includes the sample table containing two headers and two data rows.

2026-11-03.headline: Microsoft Entra Security Operator loses default threat-policy and Tenant Allow/Block List access in December
2026-11-03.overview: Starting in December 2026, Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will update Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role, removing default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List. A separate URBAC expansion adds email preview and download access for alerts involving potentially malicious URL clicks. Endpoint guidance also sharpens local AI-agent discovery limits and prerequisites, while Sentinel guidance documents MCP-assisted triage querying.
2026-11-03.adminImpact: Before the December 2026 rollout, identify workflows that depend on the Security Operator role's email threat-policy or Tenant Allow/Block List access and manually assign permissions where continued access is required. Verify that analysts have the appropriate URBAC email-content permission for message preview or download. For local-agent investigations, check the documented Defender versions and Security for AI and Exposure Management permissions; enable antivirus active mode and real-time protection when MCP server configuration discovery is needed.

keyChanges.title: Security Operator RBAC mapping will remove default email-policy access
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will update the Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role beginning in December 2026. Default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List will be removed, so organizations needing continued access must manually assign permissions.

keyChanges.title: URBAC email-content access expands to malicious URL-click alerts
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender now includes alerts related to potentially malicious URL clicks in its expanded email-content permission support. Analysts with the appropriate permission can preview and download emails from four alert types.

keyChanges.title: Local-agent inventory guidance clarifies what discovery proves
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Endpoint guidance states that observing an agent process can create an inventory entry without a prompt or service permission, and that discovery does not prove active use or successful access. It also adds minimum Defender versions and Unified RBAC permissions for viewing inventory and the attack surface graph.

keyChanges.title: MCP server discovery now has explicit endpoint prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Local Agent Discovery Overview distinguishes process-based discovery from VS Code extension collection on Windows and macOS. It states that MCP server configuration discovery requires antivirus active mode and real-time protection, and removes the macOS preview note from the guidance.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel guidance documents MCP-based triage collection
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel What's New guidance now describes using the Sentinel MCP triage collection to discover data, list available Advanced Hunting tables, and run hunting queries in the built-in data lake.

2026-11-04.headline: GCC AI-agent scope and incident similarity sharpen Defender admin guidance
2026-11-04.overview: This was a guidance-heavy period rather than a broad rollout: Defender XDR updates spell out GCC AI-agent coverage and add investigation context around similar cases, similar incidents, and recommended correlations. Office 365 Attack Simulation Training guidance now sets expectations for delayed training assignments and follow-up email, while Endpoint release notes identify macOS 101.26092.0012 and its documented fixes. A Sentinel MCP server entry only revises wording for the run hunting query tool, with no administrator action indicated.
2026-11-04.adminImpact: GCC administrators can check capability boundaries before relying on AI-agent security features. Incident responders can use similarity and correlation views for context while retaining separate ownership, status, and lifecycle where stated. Simulation administrators should allow for delayed assignments and notifications and may add the suggested notice to custom landing pages. Endpoint administrators can use the macOS release details to identify the build and review the package-scanning improvement; no action is stated.

keyChanges.title: GCC support boundaries are explicit for AI agent inventory
keyChanges.detail: The Defender XDR AI Agent Inventory article now says GCC supports agent discovery and inventory, but not agent risk assessment, security recommendations, or the attack surface graph. GCC administrators can use this scope to determine which AI-agent security capabilities are available.

keyChanges.title: Similar cases guidance adds shared-alert and entity context
keyChanges.detail: Investigate Incident Cases now documents opening the Similar cases page, reviewing similarity reasons, and viewing shared alerts and entities. Investigators can use that context to compare handling and identify recurring patterns.

keyChanges.title: Recommended correlations broaden the attack view without merging incidents
keyChanges.detail: The Recommended correlations filter includes incidents that are not correlated into the current incident, while a Summary-tab card explains potential attack relationships. Related incidents retain their own ownership, status, and lifecycle until merged.

keyChanges.title: Attack Simulation Training guidance flags delays after interactions
keyChanges.detail: The simulations guidance says new training assignments and the follow-up notification email may take time to appear after a simulation interaction. It links to end-user notification details and suggests adding a custom landing-page message about the delay.

keyChanges.title: macOS 101.26092.0012 release notes document package-scanning improvements
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint release notes list macOS version 101.26092.0012 with its release, engine, and signature versions, plus bug and performance fixes and optimized memory usage during package scanning. No administrator action is stated.

2026-11-05.headline: Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 adds Move to Quarantine in late November
2026-11-05.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 is scheduled to gain a remediation action that moves suspicious messages from user mailboxes into Defender quarantine. Defender for Cloud guidance also tightens the operational picture for Arc-enabled SQL Server: proxy support, extension versioning, manual updates, and resource exclusion procedures are now documented. Endpoint changes mainly improve Linux investigation guidance.
2026-11-05.adminImpact: Review Defender for Office 365 remediation policies and role assignments before the late-November rollout, although no action is required. For Arc-enabled SQL Server, verify the applicable extension version, network path, update procedure, and exclusion controls before expanding coverage. Linux investigators can use the documented Client Analyzer data in investigation packages.

keyChanges.title: Move to Quarantine is coming to Defender for Office 365 Plan 2
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says Plan 2 will add a remediation action that moves suspicious email from user mailboxes into Defender quarantine. Rollout begins in late November 2026; no action is required, but policy and role reviews are recommended.

keyChanges.title: Arc proxy SQL support is documented for Defender for SQL extension 2.0.3585.403
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Cloud release notes state that Azure Arc SQL Server instances with Arc proxy enabled are supported with Defender for SQL extension version 2.0.3585.403. The version is available for manual update, automatic rollout has not started, and Arc proxy can route outbound communication for organizations without direct internet access.

keyChanges.title: Defender for SQL gets documented manual update workflows across Azure management interfaces
keyChanges.detail: A new procedure page covers updating the Defender for SQL extension on Azure Arc-enabled servers and Azure VMs through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, scripts, or REST APIs. It also documents prerequisites, version verification, and the extensions in scope, excluding the SQL IaaS extension and Azure Connected Machine agent from this update workflow.

keyChanges.title: SQL exclusion guidance separates Arc servers from Azure VMs
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance provides separate procedures for Arc-enabled servers and Azure VMs, including Arc extension block or allow lists and an Azure Policy deny assignment. It states that these controls do not uninstall existing extensions or change subscription-level Defender settings; administrators excluding a resource should configure the applicable restriction before uninstalling the extension.

keyChanges.title: Linux investigation packages now include Defender for Endpoint Client Analyzer data
keyChanges.detail: Updated Endpoint guidance says Linux investigation packages include Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Client Analyzer diagnostics alongside system information, covering installation, configuration, service health, logs, and connectivity.

2026-11-06.headline: Full-management transfer guidance arrives as Defender Endpoint iOS 1.1.82260102 improves slow-network reliability
2026-11-06.overview: The period brought two substantive administrator updates: new Defender for Cloud guidance for moving Azure subscriptions or management groups into full Defender portal management, and updated Endpoint release information for an iOS build released November 3, 2026.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating a Defender for Cloud transfer should review its one-way nature, DWU billing, and loss of existing resource-level plan configurations before confirming. Endpoint teams can use the iOS release details for deployment tracking and connectivity or diagnostic troubleshooting; no specific action is prescribed.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud documents Azure moves into full portal management
keyChanges.detail: New guidance covers transferring subscriptions or management groups from Azure portal management to full Defender portal management. It describes transition stages, prerequisites, and post-transfer behavior. Before confirming a move, administrators should account for the one-way transfer, DWU billing, and loss of existing resource-level plan configurations.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint release notes identify iOS version 1.1.82260102
keyChanges.detail: The updated release information records iOS platform version 1.1.82260102, released November 3, 2026. The build improves redirected-network reliability on slow or low-bandwidth networks and updates translations for advanced diagnostic settings.

2026-11-08.headline: Defender regional coverage revisions and Threat Analytics PDF exports sharpen admin guidance
2026-11-08.overview: Three Microsoft Learn updates affect two Defender areas. Defender for Cloud’s Data Security Posture Prepare page updates AWS S3 and GCP supported-region lists and adds explicit unsupported-region lists. Its Regional Availability page also revises Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud availability lists and renames sensitivity scan sections to sensitive data discovery. Defender XDR’s Threat Analytics guidance now describes exporting reports from the Microsoft Defender portal to PDF, including threat context, analyst analysis, images, hyperlinks, and related intelligence when available.
2026-11-08.adminImpact: Administrators should use the revised regional lists when assessing AWS S3, GCP, Azure, and sensitive data discovery support. Threat Analytics users can save reports for offline review and sharing; these documentation updates alone require no configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Data Security Posture Prepare adds explicit unsupported AWS S3 and GCP region lists
keyChanges.detail: The page updates supported-region lists for AWS S3 and GCP and adds explicit lists of unsupported AWS S3 and GCP regions. Administrators should use the revised coverage when assessing resource support; no action is required by this change alone.

keyChanges.title: Regional Availability renames sensitive-data sections and revises cloud region lists
keyChanges.detail: The page renames sensitivity scan sections to sensitive data discovery and revises supported and unsupported region lists for Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud scenarios. Use the revised lists when assessing where sensitive data discovery is available.

keyChanges.title: Threat Analytics guidance details Microsoft Defender portal PDF report export
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now describes exporting reports to PDF, including threat context, analyst analysis, images, hyperlinks, and related intelligence when available. Administrators can save reports for offline review and sharing.

2026-11-09.headline: Unified RBAC guidance now requires both Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online toggles
2026-11-09.overview: The supplied period is documentation-led, with the strongest administrator impact concentrated in RBAC prerequisites and Microsoft Sentinel operating procedures. Multiple Office 365 policy articles now state that both the Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online permissions toggles under Email & collaboration must be Active for the documented Unified RBAC scenarios. Sentinel guidance marks direct analytics-rule playbook invocation as deprecated, details unified portal data-management controls, and separates Azure RBAC from Defender unified RBAC for playbooks. The Exposure Management exemptions page is now explicitly labeled preview.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Review both Office 365 permissions toggles when assessing or troubleshooting relevant portal access. For Sentinel alert-trigger playbooks invoked by analytics rules, configure automation rules so alerts continue to trigger them automatically. For the unified data-management experience, verify URBAC Data (manage) and equivalent workspace permissions, while accounting for its commercial-cloud scope and table-management limitations. Apply Azure roles to Logic App playbooks and Defender unified RBAC permissions to generated playbooks as applicable.

keyChanges.title: Office 365 policy guidance standardizes a two-toggle Unified RBAC prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The Connection Filter Policies guidance changes from requiring only the Defender for Office 365 toggle to requiring both the Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online permissions toggles under Email & collaboration to be Active. The same prerequisite now appears across the supplied anti-spam, anti-malware, anti-phishing, outbound spam, quarantine, Safe Attachments, and Safe Links guidance.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel marks direct analytics-rule playbook invocation as deprecated
keyChanges.detail: Alert-trigger playbooks and their Microsoft Sentinel Alert triggers remain supported, but direct invocation from analytics rules is deprecated. The revised procedure uses automation rules for alerts generated by one or multiple analytics rules.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel documents unified portal tabs for data and retention management
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now covers connector and table management, transformations, and ingestion-health monitoring in the unified Defender portal through Overview, Connectors, and Tables tabs. It also specifies URBAC Data (manage) and equivalent workspace permissions, limits the experience to commercial cloud, and identifies table-management limitations.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel playbook guidance separates Defender and Azure permission models
keyChanges.detail: The article distinguishes Microsoft Defender SOC Logic Apps and generated playbooks from Sentinel connector Logic Apps. Logic App playbooks require appropriate Azure roles, while generated playbooks require Defender unified RBAC permissions and no Azure roles; investigation-page access is also documented.

keyChanges.title: Exposure Management exemptions guidance now carries explicit preview labeling
keyChanges.detail: The Manage exemptions page title and heading now include “(preview),” making the preview designation explicit in the documented capability. Its custom metadata was also changed and an embedded screenshot was removed.

2026-11-10.headline: Multi-recipient Defender for Office 365 policies switch to OR matching when modified
2026-11-10.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is scheduled to change multi-recipient threat-policy inclusion from Match all (AND) to Match any (OR) in December 2026 when an affected policy is modified. That can expand policy scope, while existing policies are not automatically converted. Other substantive guidance covers a 100 MiB limit for portal retrieval of quarantined files, verdict enforcement for certain quarantined mail, preview-scoped Azure security tasks in the Defender portal, and consolidated Sentinel connector-health monitoring. Most remaining updates refine terminology, headings, links, metadata, and navigation across Defender XDR and Identity.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: Review threat-protection policies that specify multiple recipient types before editing them in December; modifying one will apply OR logic and may broaden its scope. For file investigations, account for the 100 MiB portal-download limit and use Collect file when the current device path is needed. Resolve the verdict before releasing malware or high-confidence phishing messages covered by the updated Office 365 guidance. Use the updated Defender portal comparison to identify Azure tasks available in preview.

keyChanges.title: Recipient matching changes from Match all to Match any on policy modification
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is scheduled to interpret multiple specified recipient types with Match any (OR), instead of Match all (AND), when a threat-protection policy is modified in December 2026. Existing policies are not auto-converted, but modifying one can expand its scope.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint guidance limits portal downloads to cloud-backed files up to 100 MiB
keyChanges.detail: The updated Respond File Alerts guidance says portal downloads use a cloud-backed copy rather than the device’s local quarantine. Cloud backup covers files up to 100 MiB; larger files remain quarantined but cannot be downloaded from the portal. Collect file retrieves the current device path and may fail if quarantine removed the original.

keyChanges.title: Quarantined malware and high-confidence phishing verdicts cannot be bypassed on release
keyChanges.detail: When MX points to Microsoft 365, the updated guidance says malware and high-confidence phishing messages quarantined under that setup cannot bypass their verdict when released. Administrators must resolve the verdict before release.

keyChanges.title: Azure Defender portal comparison adds four preview-scoped security tasks
keyChanges.detail: The updated comparison lists Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark, security policies, exemptions, and regulatory compliance assessments as available in preview for Azure environments in the Defender portal.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel guidance consolidates connector-health checks in Data & connectors
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance describes the Defender portal’s Data & connectors Overview tab for reviewing connector counts, ingestion volume and growth, errors, table fluctuations, and ingestion latency, with links to connector and table details.

2026-11-11.headline: Cloud Apps guidance now lists four admin assignments as unavailable in new configurations
2026-11-11.overview: The most consequential update concerns Defender for Cloud Apps: App/instance admin, User group admin, Cloud Discovery global admin, and Cloud Discovery report admin assignments cannot be used in new configurations, while existing configurations remain supported. Other substantive updates document AI-agent runtime protection limitations, a possible repeat-quarantine path in Defender for Office 365, a revised MDASH scan recommendation, and Exchange-dependent SACL guidance.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Administrators creating new Cloud Apps configurations must account for the four unavailable assignment types; existing configurations require no change. Administrators evaluating AI-agent runtime protection should interpret Audit-mode alerts and Block-mode behavior using the documented limitations. Teams using the affected Defender for Office 365 routing topology should account for possible repeat quarantine and submit the initial message version to Microsoft. MDASH administrators should note the MAI Cyber (Preview) recommendation, while identity administrators should use current or historical Exchange presence to determine whether Configuration partition SACL auditing applies.

keyChanges.title: Four Cloud Apps admin assignments are unavailable for new configurations
keyChanges.detail: The guidance states that App/instance admin, User group admin, Cloud Discovery global admin, and Cloud Discovery report admin assignments cannot be used in new configurations. Existing configurations remain supported.

keyChanges.title: AI-agent runtime protection guidance adds Audit and Block-mode limitations
