keyChanges.detail: Audit mode may incorrectly report a prompt injection block. In Block mode, Claude Code may continue processing a tool response after a reported block; a post-tool-response block cannot undo actions already completed.

keyChanges.title: Common Attachments routing can trigger quarantine after message release
keyChanges.detail: Messages quarantined by the Common Attachments Filter may be quarantined again after release because of the return mail-flow path. The updated submission guidance says to submit the initial message version to Microsoft.

keyChanges.title: MDASH guidance recommends MAI Cyber Preview for scan configuration
keyChanges.detail: The exposure management guidance now recommends MAI Cyber (Preview) as the scan configuration for MDASH.

keyChanges.title: Exchange presence or history defines Configuration partition SACL scope
keyChanges.detail: Configuration partition SACL auditing applies to environments that currently have or previously had Microsoft Exchange. Administrators should use Exchange presence or history when determining whether the configuration applies.

2026-11-12.headline: Defender for Office 365 localizes default Mark and notify emails by Outlook language
2026-11-12.overview: The most consequential update is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice that the default Mark and notify email template will follow users’ Outlook language settings, with global rollout stated to start in June 2026. The six Learn updates otherwise form a terminology and navigation pass: Identity guidance now uses identity security in Microsoft Defender, Cloud Apps guidance uses SaaS security terminology in Microsoft Defender, and affected pages refine portal routes and permissions links.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: No action is required for the localized default template; message classification and custom templates are unchanged. Administrators consulting the affected guidance should use the updated identity-security and SaaS-security terminology. For action accounts, follow Settings > Identities > General > Manage action accounts; remediation guidance now points to the Defender portal and clearer required-permissions links.

keyChanges.title: Default Mark and notify templates will follow Outlook language
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will localize the default “Mark and notify” email template based on each user’s Outlook language settings. The Message Center notice says global rollout starts in June 2026; message classification and custom templates do not change.

keyChanges.title: Manage Action Accounts guidance now gives the Defender portal path
keyChanges.detail: The documented navigation path is now Settings > Identities > General > Manage action accounts, with updated formatting for the Create new account button.

keyChanges.title: Identity role-group guidance adopts Microsoft Defender terminology
keyChanges.detail: The role-groups page title, description, and introductory guidance now refer to identity security capabilities in Microsoft Defender rather than only Defender for Identity. Two ontology links were also added.

keyChanges.title: SaaS admin-access guidance now uses Microsoft Defender terminology
keyChanges.detail: The Configure SaaS security admin access article’s title, description, headings, and introductory text now refer to SaaS security capabilities in Microsoft Defender rather than only Defender for Cloud Apps, including its guidance on Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra administrator roles.

keyChanges.title: Identity remediation guidance points to the Defender portal
keyChanges.detail: The Remediation Actions page now states that identity remediation actions are performed in the Defender portal and uses shorter links to required-permissions guidance for Disable, Enable, Revoke session, and Force password change.

2026-11-13.headline: Defender XDR documents a Teams synthetic-media hunting table
2026-11-13.overview: The period's strongest addition is documentation for the SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents advanced-hunting table, covering Microsoft Teams synthetic-media detections and investigation fields. Endpoint's AI Agent Runtime Protection guidance is more operationally specific: it separates agent-native and network inspection, defines support-matrix requirements, and maps both settings to 0 (Disabled), 1 (Block), and 2 (Audit). Identity migration wording also removes a domain-controller-only limitation statement, while threat-actor naming entries were revised.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: Queries against the Teams synthetic-media table require Defender for Office 365 and an approved detection engine. Administrators testing AI Agent Runtime Protection should match the inspection method, agent mode, and minimum version to the support matrix and use the documented numeric values. Migration teams should review the revised Sensor V3 guidance; no configuration change or deadline is stated.

keyChanges.title: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents documents Teams deepfake investigation fields
keyChanges.detail: The new Defender XDR advanced-hunting table covers Microsoft Teams synthetic-media detection events and exposes severity, confidence, maliciousness, source, user, and detection-provider details. Results require Defender for Office 365 and an approved detection engine.

keyChanges.title: AI Agent Runtime Protection now specifies numeric policy values
keyChanges.detail: The configuration guidance states that both settings use 0 for Disabled, 1 for Block, and 2 for Audit.

keyChanges.title: Runtime-protection testing now separates agent-native and network inspection
keyChanges.detail: The demonstration guide now uses a support matrix covering inspection methods, agent modes, and minimum versions. It distinguishes agent-native inspection (AiAgentProtection) from network inspection (AiAgentNetworkInspection), removes Beta Channel update-configuration steps, and adds known-issues guidance.

keyChanges.title: Threat-actor naming tables revise aliases and affiliations
keyChanges.detail: The table adds or revises aliases, affiliations, origins, and references, including new associations for Citrine Sleet, Midnight Blizzard, and Storm-2603; an entry for Storm-2195; and updated classifications for Storm-1249, Storm-2227, and Storm-3069.

keyChanges.title: Sensor V3 migration guidance removes a domain-controller-only statement
keyChanges.detail: Troubleshooting wording now refers to Defender for Endpoint sensor onboarding and removes the statement that in-place migration is supported only for domain controllers. Two ontology links were also updated.

2026-11-14.headline: Per-feature Defender preview controls and expanded Sentinel region guidance
2026-11-14.overview: The most consequential addition is a Defender for Endpoint portal control for selected public-preview features, allowing tenant-wide or safe-deployment-channel rollout. Sentinel updates mainly sharpen operational guidance: the documented data-lake region list is broader, data-lake retention now has an explicit supported-region requirement, and ASIM parser documentation better distinguishes parser types and field-retention behavior.
2026-11-14.adminImpact: Endpoint administrators can stage selected preview features and use the documented key-based offboarding workflow. Sentinel administrators should recheck data-residency and retention plans against the supported-region guidance and use the revised ASIM tables when selecting parsers or preserving unmapped fields.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint adds individual preview-feature controls
keyChanges.detail: A new Defender portal page lets administrators enable or disable selected public-preview features tenant-wide or by safe deployment channel. Features are off by default unless the tenant participated in the private preview, and the existing Preview features setting must be enabled first.

keyChanges.title: Key-based Defender offboarding is documented alongside the existing file method
keyChanges.detail: The deployment-tool guidance describes generating a tool with a Defender portal offboarding key, setting key expiration, and using interactive or quiet command-line offboarding. The key cannot be viewed again and works only with its generated tool; the .offboarding-file method remains available.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel’s documented data-lake region list expands
keyChanges.detail: The geographical-availability guidance now includes additional data-lake-supported regions, including Canada East, Brazil, East Asia, Japan West, Korea, UAE Central, France South, Norway, Switzerland West, UK West, and more Australian regions.

keyChanges.title: Data-lake retention now explicitly requires a supported workspace region
keyChanges.detail: The table-tier and retention guidance now states that a workspace must be in a supported region to use data-lake retention. Administrators should verify regional support before planning or enabling the capability.

keyChanges.title: ASIM parser guidance separates query-time and ingestion-time use
keyChanges.detail: The ASIM parser tables are reorganized with links to parser definitions, native normalized entries, and additional data sources. The guidance also clarifies that pack=true retains unmapped fields in AdditionalFields and identifies whether an ingestion-time definition exists.

2025-12-29.headline: Google Workspace lacks Enterprise Edge DLP scans while Defender for Identity adds assessments
2025-12-29.overview: The most consequential updates document a protection gap and expand identity-risk coverage. Cloud Apps guidance now says Google Workspace in the Enterprise Edge browser lacks in-browser protection, Secure Edge Session Controls, and real-time DLP file scans, while Defender for Identity’s January 2026 release notes add assessments for service accounts in privileged groups and accounts in built-in Operator Groups, including direct, indirect, and nested membership. Endpoint changes are mainly procedural: per-rule ASR exclusions, platform-specific EDR testing, and the permission requirement for undoing contain-user actions.
2025-12-29.adminImpact: Review whether Google Workspace users in Enterprise Edge require controls that are unavailable in that combination. Use the new Defender for Identity assessments to review privileged or unnecessary access. For Endpoint operations, follow the relevant EDR procedure and verify that TCP port 80 is available before server testing; use the documented per-rule ASR exclusion methods and confirm that operators who need to undo contain-user actions have the required Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise Edge guidance documents Google Workspace protection gaps
keyChanges.detail: The Cloud Apps known-issues entry states that Google Workspace in Enterprise Edge does not support in-browser protection, Secure Edge Session Controls, or real-time DLP file scans. Browser sessions use fallback authentication suffixes instead of Secure Edge.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity adds privileged-access assessment coverage
keyChanges.detail: The January 2026 release notes add assessments for service accounts in privileged groups and accounts in built-in Operator Groups, covering direct, indirect, and nested membership. Administrators can use them to identify elevated or unnecessary access and review exposure.

keyChanges.title: ASR guidance states that exclusions can be configured per rule
keyChanges.detail: The enablement guidance now states that Group Policy, PowerShell, and Intune can configure exclusions for specific attack surface reduction rules. Group Policy and PowerShell users can therefore use targeted per-rule exclusions rather than exclusions applied across all rules.

keyChanges.title: EDR detection testing now distinguishes client and server procedures
keyChanges.detail: Windows client instructions use PowerShell to create and rename an EICAR test file. Windows server instructions retain the download-and-run test and add a TCP port 80 prerequisite with a connectivity check.

keyChanges.title: Undoing contain-user actions requires Global Administrator
keyChanges.detail: Response-action guidance now states that undoing contain-user actions requires membership in the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra permissions, alongside least-privilege guidance. Operators without that role cannot perform the operation.

2026-01-05.headline: Defender for Office 365 quarantine rollout brings recipient-level lists and per-user releases
2026-01-05.overview: The week’s clearest operational changes are a January–March 2026 Defender for Office 365 quarantine rollout and an opt-in Windows event-auditing setup feature for Defender for Identity unified sensors v3.x. Vulnerability Management reporting is also being narrowed, while Exposure Management content now covers cloud software inventory. A new Teams blocking procedure adds concrete limits and prerequisites. Most of the remaining update volume is documentation maintenance—especially Endpoint API URLs, OData examples, navigation, and table formatting—rather than broad feature announcements.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: Update quarantine runbooks for recipient-specific listings and per-user releases; no end-user change is stated. Decide whether to enable the unified-sensor auditing option through the UI or Graph API during the January rollout. Rebaseline expectations for Vulnerability Management reports, particularly the 30-day history and Device group-only filtering, with Government cloud timing in late January. For Teams blocks, validate settings, permissions, and entry limits before configuring. Integration owners should review affected Endpoint API references for the move from the old Security Center hostname to `api.security.microsoft.com`.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Office 365 quarantine becomes recipient-specific for administrators
keyChanges.detail: Message Center notice MC1171845 says the January–March 2026 rollout will list quarantined messages by individual recipient and require releases per user, alongside backend durability improvements. End-user behavior is unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Unified sensors v3.x get opt-in automatic Windows event auditing
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Identity unified sensors v3.x will offer automatic configuration of Windows event-auditing settings from mid-January 2026. Administrators can enable it in the UI or through Graph API; rollout is scheduled to complete by the end of January.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Management report history and filters are reduced
keyChanges.detail: The updated January What's New entry says the report removes the Windows 10/11 version-over-time section, limits filtering to Device group, and reduces history to the last 30 days. Government cloud customers are scheduled to see the changes in late January 2026.

keyChanges.title: Exposure Management documents cloud software inventory for exposure analysis
keyChanges.detail: January 2026 Exposure Management content now covers cloud software inventory, including cloud software, application versions, installed assets, and related vulnerabilities. Administrators can use the inventory to understand exposure and prioritize vulnerability assessments.

keyChanges.title: Teams blocking guidance sets Tenant Allow/Block List limits
keyChanges.detail: A new Office 365 procedure explains blocking Teams domains and email addresses from the Microsoft Defender portal. It identifies required Teams settings and permissions, caps the list at 4,000 domain entries and 200 user entries, and documents block effects and timing.

2026-01-12.headline: Endpoint DLP alerting retires March 23 as macOS and ASR guidance shifts
2026-01-12.overview: Microsoft will retire endpoint-sensitive data alerting in the Defender portal on March 23, 2026. Existing Defender alert policies will stop generating alerts after that date, with Microsoft directing organizations to Microsoft Purview DLP for endpoint alerting, enforcement, and investigation. Other notable updates cover new macOS extension policy requirements, revised Microsoft 365 connector setup defaults, expanded Defender for Identity sensor guidance, and a reorganized attack surface reduction enablement path.
2026-01-12.adminImpact: Treat March 23 as the key migration deadline and move endpoint sensitive-data alerting, enforcement, and investigation to Microsoft Purview DLP. Use the Intune settings catalog and System Extension payload for new macOS extension policies; existing policies can continue working. Review Microsoft 365 connector settings and required Entra permissions, inspect Defender for Identity RPC-auditing alerts, and update ASR rollout runbooks against the new prerequisites and deployment methods.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint DLP sensitive-data alerting has a March 23 retirement deadline
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft will retire endpoint-sensitive data alerting in the Defender portal on March 23, 2026. Existing Defender alert policies will stop generating alerts after that date; Microsoft directs organizations to Microsoft Purview DLP for alerting, enforcement, and investigation of endpoint sensitive-data activity.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud Apps will change defaults for new Microsoft 365 connectors
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the January 2026 Microsoft 365 connector configuration update will add a clearer layout and new default values for new connectors. Existing connectors remain unchanged; administrators should review current settings and verify that required Microsoft Entra permissions are enabled.

keyChanges.title: New macOS extension policies must use the Intune Settings Catalog
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance states that Intune policy support for creating new macOS extension policies was deprecated in August 2024, service release 2048. Existing policies continue to work, while new policies must use the Intune settings catalog and System Extension payload.

keyChanges.title: Attack surface reduction guidance now specifies prerequisites and five deployment paths
keyChanges.detail: The new enablement article covers Intune, mobile device management, Configuration Manager, Group Policy, and PowerShell. Using the full attack surface reduction rule feature set requires Defender Antivirus as the primary antivirus—not passive or disabled—along with real-time protection, cloud-delivered protection, and Cloud Protection network connectivity. Microsoft 365 E5 is recommended but not required.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity guidance adds RPC-auditing health and sensor configuration details
keyChanges.detail: The updated What's New content adds a health alert for v3.x sensors with missing or incorrectly configured enhanced RPC auditing and describes a gradual rollout of automatic Windows event-auditing configuration for new and existing sensors.

keyChanges.title: Android app update deadline

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity adds a missing-traffic health alert
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Identity now reports a health alert when expected domain-controller network traffic is missing. The alert appears in sensor health tabs and helps identify traffic-collection problems that can reduce visibility.

keyChanges.title: A new health issue flags missing domain-controller Windows events
keyChanges.detail: The new sensor health issue, "No Windows events received from domain controller," identifies event-collection gaps that can affect detections. It is available now and requires no pre-rollout action.

keyChanges.title: macOS performance guidance adds a process-specific investigation workflow
keyChanges.detail: Updated Defender for Endpoint on macOS guidance covers high resource use by wdavdaemon or wdavdaemon_enterprise with Activity Monitor or top checks, hot-event-source collection, Client Analyzer data, coexistence checks, and support information. It also states that antivirus exclusions do not suppress EDR or other Endpoint Security events.

keyChanges.title: NetExt troubleshooting separates enforcement from extension-wide failures
keyChanges.detail: The revised macOS Network Extension guidance distinguishes Network Protection enforcement problems from issues occurring whenever NetExt runs, and adds health checks, a test matrix, diagnostic commands, and collection requirements. It warns that disabling NetExt reduces network visibility and disables dependent capabilities.

2026-08-24.headline: Defender AIR moves to always-on protection before its September 1 manual-trigger deadline
2026-08-24.overview: The period’s most consequential change moves Microsoft Defender for Endpoint automated investigation and response from a manually triggered, standalone experience into always-on antivirus protection. Defender for Cloud Apps also has a firm App Governance role-support retirement deadline, while Defender XDR is staging two unified identity capabilities. One Attack Surface Reduction Rules example received a precise identifier correction.
2026-08-24.adminImpact: Prioritize AIR playbook and script remediation before September 1, 2026. keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint AIR manual triggering is removed by early September
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint will remove manual triggering and the standalone automated investigation and response experience by early September 2026. keyChanges.title: App Governance retires Cloud Application Administrator support on September 26
keyChanges.detail: Support for the Cloud Application Administrator role in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps App Governance will retire on September 26, 2026. keyChanges.title: Defender XDR unifies response actions across identity accounts
keyChanges.detail: A unified workflow will let security teams manage identity response actions such as disabling accounts or forcing password changes across linked accounts. keyChanges.title: Identity Timeline gains a unified cross-source activity and alert view
keyChanges.detail: The Identity page’s Timeline tab will provide a chronological view of identity activities and alerts from multiple Microsoft security sources, with improved context, filtering, and automatic updates. keyChanges.title: ASR command example corrects a rule identifier ending in `...e5b`

2026-08-31.headline: Sentinel SAP connector retirement sets a September 14 migration deadline
2026-08-31.overview: The clearest operational deadline is Sentinel’s permanent retirement of the containerized SAP connector agent on September 14, 2026. 2026-08-31.adminImpact: Administrators running the containerized SAP connector should migrate to the agentless connector before September 14 and use the agentless option for new systems. Defender XDR teams should decide whether to keep the new DLP behavior default or disable it to preserve DLP alerts in the Defender XDR incident queue. Linux administrators should check the Defender version requirement before using audit mode, and identity teams deploying sensors only on non-domain-controller servers must install at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller and use manual activation.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel will disable the containerized SAP connector on September 14
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the containerized SAP connector agent will be permanently retired and disabled on September 14, 2026. New deployments should use the agentless connector, and existing deployments should migrate before SAP logs stop; existing analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks remain functional with the agentless path.

keyChanges.title: Defender XDR will default Purview DLP alerts to behaviors October 12
keyChanges.detail: Starting October 12, 2026, Microsoft Defender XDR will treat Microsoft Purview DLP alerts as behaviors by default, reducing alert volume while keeping DLP data available in Advanced Hunting and Purview. Administrators can disable the rule to retain those alerts in the Defender XDR incident queue.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Office 365 rolls out email prompt-injection protection
keyChanges.detail: The protection detects and quarantines malicious email content aimed at AI assistants. It applies to organizations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5, with automatic high-confidence threat quarantine enabled by default as rollout continues through October 2026.

keyChanges.title: Linux guidance specifies four Defender antivirus enforcement levels
keyChanges.detail: The updated Defender for Endpoint on Linux guidance documents four enforcement levels, identifies passive mode as the default, and adds audit mode as a preview capability. Audit mode requires Defender for Endpoint version 101.26062.0007 or later, and the article adds a command for checking the active enforcement level.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity v3.x covers preview activation on non-domain controllers
keyChanges.detail: Version 3.x sensor guidance now includes eligible AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers that are not domain controllers. Activation on those servers is in preview, requires manual activation, and does not support automatic activation or migration; deployments limited to those servers also need at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller.

2026-09-07.headline: Sentinel normalization guidance now prohibits cross-table enrichment and preserves record cardinality
2026-09-07.overview: The period’s most consequential update was revised Sentinel parser guidance: parsers are limited to their declared source table, one normalized output per source record, and scalar or local static mappings. Cross-table enrichment, watchlists, multi-value expansion, joins, aggregation, and deduplication are explicitly excluded. Companion AI-agent guidance permits query-local lookup mappings only when keys are unique. Defender XDR also added detailed advanced-hunting graph guidance, while seven Azure Storage alert entries now use Informational severity. Other changes were mainly editorial, with added troubleshooting steps for the Sensor v3.x RPC Audit Misconfigured alert.
2026-09-07.adminImpact: Review custom Sentinel parsers and connectors against the documented source-table, record-cardinality, and enrichment limits. For AI-agent parser creation, use unique lookup keys and plan for record-by-record normalization; no required configuration change is stated. Use the revised Informational labels when reviewing documented Azure Storage alerts. Administrators troubleshooting the Identity health alert should follow the added resolution guidance, including verification of Unified Sensor RPC Audit configuration. The Linux formatting, Regex scope, filesystem-layout, and connector-link edits require no action.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel parser guidance draws strict normalization boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance limits parsers to the declared source table and one normalized output per source record, using scalar or local static mappings. It explicitly excludes cross-table enrichment, watchlists, multi-value expansion, joins, aggregation, and deduplication; source filtering must use fields from the current event.

keyChanges.title: AI-agent parser guidance preserves record-by-record output
keyChanges.detail: Parser-creation skills are described as normalizing each source record independently while preserving record cardinality. Query-local datatable or lookup mappings are allowed only when lookup keys are unique; same-table and cross-table event enrichment are not used.

keyChanges.title: Advanced hunting receives dedicated graph-mapping guidance
keyChanges.detail: A new page explains how to prepare query results, configure graph nodes and edges, apply relationship conditions, and use recognized entity types and identifiers for Defender enrichment.

keyChanges.title: Advanced hunting results guidance expands visual relationship workflows
keyChanges.detail: The updated article documents mapping results to nodes and edges through Builder or JSON, then exploring entity enrichment, relationship details, folding, and mapping edits without writing a graph-specific query.

keyChanges.title: Seven Azure Storage alert entries now show Informational severity
keyChanges.detail: The documented severity for seven Azure Storage alerts changed from High, Medium, or Low variants to Informational. Administrators should use the revised labels when reviewing and prioritizing these documented alerts.

2026-09-14.headline: Advanced Hunting adds Teams MessageContents table for message investigations
2026-09-14.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is introducing a new MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting for Microsoft Teams messages. The table will let authorized security analysts query message snippets and metadata during threat investigations, with worldwide rollout scheduled from late September through mid-October 2026.
2026-09-14.adminImpact: Verify that intended analysts have the appropriate permissions to access the new table, and account for the rollout window when planning Teams threat-hunting workflows.

keyChanges.title: New MessageContents table for Teams hunting
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Hunting will expose a MessageContents table containing Teams message snippets and metadata for authorized analysts investigating threats. The capability rolls out worldwide from late September to mid-October 2026 and requires appropriate permissions.

2026-09-21.headline: Teams message flyout adds Microsoft submission and sender-blocking actions
2026-09-21.overview: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will enhance the Teams message entity flyout by late September 2026. The updated workflow will let security administrators submit messages to Microsoft and block senders or domains from the same investigation flow.
2026-09-21.adminImpact: Plan 1 and Plan 2 customers can use the streamlined Teams message investigation workflow without making configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Remediation actions added to the Teams message entity flyout
keyChanges.detail: By late September 2026, the flyout will support submitting Teams messages to Microsoft and blocking senders or domains in one workflow.

2026-09-28.headline: Foundational CSPM moves to opt-in while XDR readies detection-source alert tuning
2026-09-28.overview: Two Defender for Cloud changes carry the clearest operational weight: Foundational CSPM will be off by default for new Azure subscriptions from 27 October, while server identification and billing counts are changing. Defender XDR guidance now separates Sentinel-only custom-detection scheduling from Defender XDR lookback behavior and announces source-specific alert tuning for preview and general availability. Identity sensor v3 deployment guidance adds a version-specific Windows update prerequisite and eligibility limits; most other entries are terminology, navigation, formatting, or procedure maintenance.
2026-09-28.adminImpact: From 27 October, enable Foundational CSPM on each new Azure subscription where its recommendations and Secure Score are needed, and review server classification and counting for billing. For custom detections, confirm the data source and lookback coverage; consider source-specific alert-tuning changes when preview opens. Before installing or upgrading sensor 3.0.8 or later for automatic RPC auditing on domain controllers, verify the Windows Server cumulative-update and eligibility requirements.

keyChanges.title: Foundational CSPM will be disabled by default on new Azure subscriptions
keyChanges.detail: Beginning 27 October 2026, new Azure subscriptions will have Foundational CSPM disabled by default. The plan remains free, while existing subscriptions and AWS and GCP environments are unaffected. Enable the plan on new subscriptions where its security recommendations and Secure Score are required.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud billing will stop counting non-server devices as Plan 1 servers
keyChanges.detail: The release notes state that Plan 1 will no longer bill desktop, workstation, and mobile devices as servers. For Plans 1 and 2, server identification will run more frequently and count deployed machines individually, which may change billed server totals.

keyChanges.title: Custom detection scheduling now depends on the data source
keyChanges.detail: Custom frequency from 5 minutes to 14 days is available only for rules based exclusively on Microsoft Sentinel data. Rules using Defender XDR data use fixed lookback periods tied to run frequency, ranging from 4 hours to 30 days. Administrators should verify the source and expected coverage when creating or reviewing rules.

keyChanges.title: XDR alert tuning will target individual detection sources
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says alert-tuning rules will be able to target specific detection sources, with public preview planned for mid-October 2026 and general availability for mid-November 2026. Existing rules will continue applying to all sources unless administrators update them; no action is needed unless finer-grained customization is wanted.

keyChanges.title: Sensor v3 deployment now has explicit update and eligibility gates
keyChanges.detail: Manual activation in preview is limited to eligible non-domain-controller AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers without an existing sensor. A July 2026 or later Windows Server cumulative update is required before installing or upgrading to sensor version 3.0.8 or later for automatic RPC auditing on domain controllers.

2026-10-05.headline: Teams QR protection and new Defender hunting tables headline the week
2026-10-05.overview: The period was documentation-heavy, with many Exposure Management entries changing only author metadata. The substantive administrator-facing changes were post-delivery Teams QR-code protection, new Defender for Office 365 hunting tables, unified server-management guidance, a Kubernetes recommendation-scope change, and a Sentinel connector for SAP BTP vulnerability findings.
2026-10-05.adminImpact: Review Teams URL-protection settings and investigation processes; no user action is required for the QR-code rollout. Track the SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults preview-to-GA transition, although no immediate action or compliance change is stated. For server workflows, review RBAC, device groups, cloud scopes, and offboarding procedures. Update KSPM triage to locate findings against workload controllers. For SAP BTP, enable API access and create dedicated client credentials; Corelight deployments now also require Reader and Microsoft Graph access alongside Monitoring Metrics Publisher.

keyChanges.title: Teams QR-code protection moves into post-delivery detection
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is extending Teams URL protection to detect malicious URLs in QR codes after delivery, warn users, and expose the activity for Advanced Hunting. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for October through November 2026, with no user action required.

keyChanges.title: SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults expand Defender hunting data
keyChanges.detail: Two new Advanced Hunting tables will provide Microsoft Defender for Office 365 email-submission visibility. Public Preview starts in early October 2026 and General Availability begins in late October 2026; the announcement states that no immediate action or compliance change is required.

keyChanges.title: Server guidance documents unified Endpoint and Defender for Servers workflows
keyChanges.detail: Updated Defender for Cloud release notes describe combined Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers data for unified inventory, cross-service investigations, Go hunt, and access through RBAC, device groups, and cloud scopes. They also document offboarding eligible servers by disabling Defender for Servers for a subscription.
keyChanges.product: Defender for Cloud and Defender for Endpoint

keyChanges.title: KSPM recommendations now target Kubernetes workload controllers
keyChanges.detail: Starting October 5, 2026, Defender for Cloud KSPM misconfiguration recommendations align with Kubernetes workload controllers rather than individual running container instances. Teams should adjust how they locate and triage these findings.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel reference adds SAP BTP vulnerability ingestion
keyChanges.detail: The Sentinel Data Connectors Reference adds a connector for SAP BTP application vulnerability findings. Using it requires API access and dedicated client credentials. The same update says Corelight deployments now require Reader and Microsoft Graph access in addition to Monitoring Metrics Publisher.

2026-10-12.headline: Defender for Identity guidance raises sensor prerequisite to September 2026 cumulative update
2026-10-12.overview: The week was dominated by documentation maintenance, but several updates have direct operational consequences. Defender for Identity deployment guidance replaces the July 2026 prerequisite with the September 2026 Windows Server cumulative update; Defender for Cloud documents a 250-snapshot scan-suspension threshold; and Cloud Apps retires two EWS-based anomaly detections on October 15. Advanced hunting guidance also moves agent data from AIAgentsInfo to unified AgentsInfo, while Endpoint release notes add concrete build and protection-behavior details.
2026-10-12.adminImpact: Prioritize Identity server readiness and migration settings; verify AWS scanner deletion permissions and clean up snapshots before the 250-snapshot threshold; remove monitoring dependencies on the retired EWS detections; update agent-related hunting queries to AgentsInfo; and review Endpoint automation for the renamed ConfigurationProtection property. The remaining changes are mainly editorial, navigational, or procedural refinements.

keyChanges.title: Sensor v3 deployment now names the September 2026 cumulative update
keyChanges.detail: The Deploy Sensor V3 guidance replaces the July 2026 Windows Server cumulative-update prerequisite with September 2026 for sensor version 3.0.10 or later. It also clarifies that v2 migration does not automatically remove workspace DSA or gMSA configuration; select the local system account option before migrating from v2.x.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud documents a 250-snapshot suspension threshold for AWS scans
keyChanges.detail: The agentless-scanning guidance says deletion authorization failures involving 250 or more Defender-tagged snapshots suspend new scans for the affected AWS scope, while snapshots continue accruing storage charges until deleted. Ensure the scanner role has ec2:DeleteSnapshot, review AWS policy restrictions, and verify cleanup after access is restored.

keyChanges.title: Two EWS anomaly detections stop generating alerts after October 15
keyChanges.detail: The App Governance Anomaly Detection Alerts page now marks two EWS-based detections Retired as of October 15, 2026. They no longer generate alerts, so administrators should not use those detections as an alerting dependency after that date.

keyChanges.title: Advanced hunting guidance moves agent data from AIAgentsInfo to AgentsInfo
keyChanges.detail: The schema update describes the transition to the unified AgentsInfo table, whose coverage extends beyond Copilot Studio-specific columns. Review and update agent-related hunting queries and schema references accordingly.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint release notes add new builds and protection-engine behavior details
keyChanges.detail: The release page now lists Platform 4.18.26090.9, Engine 1.1.26090.9, and security intelligence 1.461.1.0, along with automatic protection-engine refresh, improved update reliability, ASR path handling, and policy-exclusion retention. Review automation that uses the renamed PowerShell property ConfigurationProtection, and validate the documented protection and ASR behavior.

2026-10-19.headline: Defender for Cloud portal guidance defines DWU billing and migration scope
2026-10-19.overview: The week’s highest-impact items are migration- and deadline-driven. Defender for Cloud guidance explains DWU billing and scope consequences for portal-managed plans, while Defender for Identity documents a 30-day opt-out before sensor v3.x activation and Windows auditing defaults. Direct server onboarding is explicitly tenant-wide, Defender XDR has a 30-day hunting-schema transition, and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 is scheduled to add Move to Quarantine worldwide in November–December 2026.
2026-10-19.adminImpact: Review Defender for Cloud migration effects before moving plan management: billing changes to Defender Workload Units, resource-level settings are not preserved, and migrated settings become view-only in the Azure portal. Treat Direct onboarding as a tenant-wide decision, check the Defender for Identity banner promptly, update AadDeviceId queries during the 30-day window, and prepare policy and training reviews for the Defender for Office 365 remediation rollout.

keyChanges.title: Portal migration changes plan billing, scope, and Azure editability
keyChanges.detail: The new guidance says moving plan management from the Azure portal to the Defender portal changes billing to Defender Workload Units (DWUs), moves configuration to tenant, management-group, or subscription scope, and may replace, consolidate, or measure plans differently. Resource-level configurations are not preserved, and migrated settings become view-only in the Azure portal.

keyChanges.title: Eligible Defender for Identity organizations get a 30-day v3.x opt-out
keyChanges.detail: Organizations with an active Defender for Identity workspace receive a banner before sensor v3.x activation and Windows auditing are enabled by default, including settings currently set to Off. Selecting Opt out within 30 days retains the current settings.

keyChanges.title: Direct server onboarding cannot target an individual pilot group
keyChanges.detail: The updated procedure states that Direct onboarding affects all eligible existing and future non-Azure servers in the same Microsoft Entra tenant. Individual-server or pilot-group selection is unsupported; prerequisites include healthy Defender for Endpoint telemetry, a matching tenant, and the required roles.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting starts the AadDeviceId schema replacement
keyChanges.detail: The AadDeviceId column is being replaced by EntraIdDeviceId. AadDeviceId remains available for 30 days, giving administrators a transition window to update Advanced Hunting queries.

keyChanges.title: Plan 2 Move to Quarantine rollout is scheduled for November–December
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 will add a Move to Quarantine remediation action that moves suspicious messages from user mailboxes into Defender quarantine. The worldwide rollout is planned from November through December 2026, with policy reviews and training updates recommended.

2026-10-26.headline: Advanced Hunting API retirement sets January migration deadline as Teams telemetry expands
2026-10-26.overview: The week’s most consequential changes center on Advanced Hunting. Microsoft announced the retirement of the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs while adding Teams message, Teams call and meeting, and email-submission data sources in Defender for Office 365. Exposure Management also made Azure posture policies and recommendation exemptions available in public preview. Many other updates were reference, metadata, or terminology edits rather than operational changes.
2026-10-26.adminImpact: Prioritize an inventory of workflows using the MDE or XDR Advanced Hunting APIs and manually migrate them to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027, ahead of the February 1 retirement. For the new hunting data sources, review required permissions and Defender for Office 365 licensing, then assess whether analyst procedures or Sentinel and event-streaming workflows should use the new tables. Azure security teams can evaluate the Exposure Management preview capabilities as appropriate.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting APIs retire February 1, 2027
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft will retire the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs on February 1, 2027. Organizations must manually migrate workflows to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027, to maintain functionality.
keyChanges.product: Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR

keyChanges.title: Teams MessageContents table adds message snippets to hunting
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Office 365 is introducing a MessageContents Advanced Hunting table for Microsoft Teams messages. Authorized security analysts can query message snippets and metadata; rollout runs from late September through mid-November 2026, and access requires specific permissions.

keyChanges.title: CallActivityEvents brings Teams calls and meetings into hunting
keyChanges.detail: The new CallActivityEvents table enables Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 teams to investigate suspicious Microsoft Teams calls and meetings using activities, initiators, organizers, and related messages. It is scheduled for worldwide availability from November 2026 and integrates with Advanced Hunting, the event streaming API, and Microsoft Sentinel.
keyChanges.product: Defender XDR and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2

keyChanges.title: SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults add email-submission visibility
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Office 365 will add SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults to Advanced Hunting. Public Preview begins in mid-November 2026, followed by General Availability in late November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Azure posture policies and recommendation exemptions enter public preview
keyChanges.detail: Exposure Management now offers public-preview posture policies and recommendation exemptions for Azure environments. Administrators can evaluate Azure resources against the Microsoft Defender for Cloud baseline, create custom posture policies, and centrally manage accepted-risk exemptions with lifecycle tracking.

2026-11-02.headline: Defender RBAC auto-enablement and Move to Quarantine set near-term priorities
2026-11-02.overview: The week’s most consequential changes affect access control and email response. Defender RBAC will auto-enable in December 2026, the Microsoft Entra Security Operator mapping will lose default access to key Defender for Office 365 controls, and Plan 2 is gaining a Move to Quarantine remediation action in late November. Most remaining updates were documentation clarifications, including sharper boundaries for local AI-agent discovery and Defender for SQL support through Azure Arc proxy.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Prioritize review of imported Defender RBAC roles before tenant activation and explicitly reassign Microsoft Entra Security Operator permissions where continued access to email threat policies or the Tenant/Allow Block List is required. No rollout action is required for Move to Quarantine, but review relevant policies and roles. For local AI-agent investigations, treat inventory as evidence that a process was observed rather than proof of active use or successful access, and verify the documented versions and permissions. For Arc SQL Server deployments, check extension versions and outbound connectivity; the supported Defender for SQL extension can be updated manually, while automatic rollout has not started.

keyChanges.title: Defender RBAC auto-enablement requires role review before activation
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Defender RBAC will be auto-enabled in the tenant starting December 2026. Existing roles will be imported for review, with activation occurring about 30 days after notification. Administrators can adjust roles as needed, and opt-out is available after activation; permissions for other Microsoft services remain unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Entra Security Operator mapping drops default MDO policy access
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, the Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role will remove default access to email threat policies and the Tenant/Allow Block List. Administrators must manually assign permissions where that access needs to continue.

keyChanges.title: Plan 2 adds Move to Quarantine for suspicious mailbox messages
keyChanges.detail: The new remediation action moves suspicious email from user mailboxes into Defender quarantine for investigation and management. Rollout begins in late November 2026. No action is required, although Microsoft recommends reviewing applicable policies and roles.

keyChanges.title: Local AI-agent guidance separates observation from proof of use
keyChanges.detail: Updated Defender for Endpoint guidance states that observing an agent process can create an inventory entry without a prompt or service permission, while discovery alone does not prove active use or successful access. The guidance also lists minimum Defender versions and Unified RBAC permissions for viewing inventory and the attack surface graph.

keyChanges.title: Arc proxy SQL coverage hinges on extension version 2.0.3585.403
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Cloud release guidance records support for Azure Arc SQL Server instances with Arc proxy enabled when the Defender for SQL extension is version 2.0.3585.403. The version is available for manual update, while automatic rollout has not started.

2026-11-09.headline: Classic Defender for Identity alerts retire as Sentinel automation and email-policy scope change
2026-11-09.overview: The period’s most consequential items are a late-November retirement of two Defender for Identity alerts, a December change to Defender for Office 365 recipient matching, and Sentinel guidance moving direct analytics-rule playbook invocation to automation rules. Microsoft also documented per-feature preview controls for Defender for Endpoint and the SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents hunting table for Teams. Much of the remaining activity refined terminology, navigation, RBAC prerequisites, and troubleshooting guidance.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Prioritize replacement detections for the retiring identity alerts and review Sentinel playbooks invoked directly by analytics rules. Assess affected Defender for Office 365 policies before modifying them because recipient scope will broaden under the new matching logic. For Endpoint preview testing, enable the existing Preview features setting first; for Teams synthetic-media investigations, confirm the Defender for Office 365 and approved detection-engine prerequisites.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Identity will retire two classic alerts by late November
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the Remote code execution attempt and pass-the-hash classic alerts will retire by late November 2026. Create custom detection rules for RCE and use Defender for Endpoint for pass-the-hash monitoring.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel deprecates direct analytics-rule invocation for alert-trigger playbooks
keyChanges.detail: Alert-trigger playbooks and their Microsoft Sentinel Alert triggers remain supported, but direct invocation from analytics rules is deprecated. Configure automation rules for alerts created by one or multiple analytics rules to preserve automatic execution.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Office 365 will broaden recipient matching from AND to OR
keyChanges.detail: A December 2026 rollout changes threat-protection policy inclusion logic from Match all (AND) to Match any (OR) when multiple recipient types are specified. Existing policies are not auto-converted, but their scope expands when modified.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint adds per-feature controls for public previews
keyChanges.detail: A new Defender portal page lets administrators enable or disable selected public preview features tenant-wide or by safe deployment channel. Features are off by default unless the tenant participated in the private preview, and the existing Preview features setting must be enabled to access the page.

keyChanges.title: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents is documented for Teams deepfake investigations
keyChanges.detail: The advanced-hunting table provides Microsoft Teams synthetic-media detection events with severity, confidence, maliciousness, source, user, and detection-provider details. Results require Defender for Office 365 and an approved detection engine.

2026-01.headline: March deadlines retire Defender endpoint DLP alerting and Android 10 support
2026-01.overview: January’s clearest administrator deadlines are March 23, when endpoint-sensitive data alerting in Microsoft Defender retires and existing Defender alert policies stop generating alerts, and March 31, when Defender for Android ends updates, security fixes, and support for Android 10. Microsoft directs endpoint DLP customers to Microsoft Purview DLP, while Android 10 fleets need upgrading or replacement. Defender XDR also introduced built-in alert-tuning rules for low-severity Office 365 alerts, with automated triage and reopening when needed; the rules become active February 5, with an opt-out window until then. Other meaningful changes include Exposure management navigation for Vulnerability Management preview customers and new onboarding-key and package-expiry controls in the Defender deployment tool. Much of the remaining supplied material is metadata, wording, or terminology maintenance rather than a broad capability rollout.
2026-01.adminImpact: Prioritize the two migrations: identify endpoint-sensitive-data alerting that still depends on the Defender portal and move it to Microsoft Purview DLP before March 23; identify Android 10 devices and upgrade or replace them before March 31. Review the Defender XDR alert-tuning rules and opt-out timing by February 5 if required. Preview Vulnerability Management customers should update portal navigation and runbooks, while deployment teams should incorporate portal-generated keys and package expiration into Defender onboarding automation.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint DLP alerting moves to Microsoft Purview by March 23
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is retiring endpoint-sensitive data alerting in the Microsoft Defender portal on March 23, 2026. Existing Defender alert policies will stop generating alerts after that date. Microsoft directs organizations to Microsoft Purview DLP for endpoint alerting, enforcement, and investigation.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Android drops Android 10 support March 31
keyChanges.detail: After March 31, 2026, Android 10 devices will no longer receive Microsoft Defender updates, security fixes, or support. Devices running Android 11 or later remain fully supported.

keyChanges.title: Built-in Defender XDR rules change low-severity Office 365 triage
keyChanges.detail: Defender XDR is introducing built-in alert-tuning rules for low-severity Office 365 alerts. The rules provide automated triage and can reopen alerts when needed; they are active from February 5, with an opt-out window until February 5 and support for multi-tenant management.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Management moves under Exposure management for preview customers
keyChanges.detail: For Microsoft Defender XDR plus Microsoft Defender for Endpoint preview customers, the Vulnerability Management section moves to Exposure management > Vulnerability management. The former Dashboard is renamed Overview, exposure metrics are integrated, and Misconfiguration and Devices secure score sections move to the new Recommendations page. Existing Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management customers continue to see Vulnerability Management directly under the Defender portal navigation.

keyChanges.title: Defender deployment packages gain onboarding-key and expiry controls
keyChanges.detail: The updated Defender deployment tool preview guidance specifies that administrators must enter a key generated on the portal onboarding page to prevent accidental onboarding. Deployment packages can be configured to expire at any point up to one year, and the guidance recommends keeping validity as short as practical; onboarding events also appear in the device timeline and advanced hunting.

2026-08.headline: Defender AIR shifts to always-on protection as September migration deadlines approach
2026-08.overview: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is replacing manual, standalone AIR with always-on antivirus integration ahead of a September 1 automation deadline. Other material administrator changes cluster in September: the Android app needs a minimum version by mid-month, Edge retires WIP and MDAG by late month, and Defender Unified RBAC begins automatic tenant activation. Defender for Cloud Apps also ends App Governance support for the Cloud Application Administrator role on September 26.
2026-08.adminImpact: Remediate AIR playbooks and scripts before September 1; update Android devices to version 1.0.9107.0101 or later by mid-September; plan Windows 10 WIP and MDAG migration; use the 30-day Unified RBAC notice to review imported Defender and Sentinel roles; and reassign affected Cloud Application Administrator users by September 25.

keyChanges.title: AIR manual triggering and the standalone experience are being removed
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint will integrate automated investigation and response into always-on antivirus protection by early September 2026. Manual triggering and the standalone AIR experience will be removed, so organizations using AIR in playbooks or scripts must update them before September 1, 2026.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint Android requires version 1.0.9107.0101 or later
keyChanges.detail: Administrators must update Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Android by mid-September 2026 to avoid mobile threat-protection disruption caused by infrastructure changes. Device owners who manage their own updates should be notified; no other configuration changes are required.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for Android

keyChanges.title: Edge retires Windows Information Protection and Application Guard support
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Edge will retire support for Windows Information Protection and Microsoft Defender Application Guard by late September 2026. These capabilities are already removed in Windows 11 version 24H2; Windows 10 deployments using them must migrate to Microsoft Purview solutions and Edge built-in security features.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge and Defender Application Guard

keyChanges.title: Defender Unified RBAC will automatically activate across tenants
keyChanges.detail: Automatic enablement begins in late September 2026 and completes by December 2026. Unified RBAC brings access management together across Defender and Sentinel workloads, imports existing roles, and provides a 30-day notification period before activation. An opt-out is available after activation, while other Microsoft permissions remain unchanged.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel

keyChanges.title: App Governance drops Cloud Application Administrator role support
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps App Governance will stop supporting the Cloud Application Administrator role on September 26, 2026. Review assignments by September 25 and reassign affected administrators to supported roles such as Security Administrator to preserve access when Unified RBAC is enabled.

2026-09.headline: Defender October deadlines reset DLP alerts, retire Linux ARM64, and enable Teams reporting
2026-09.overview: September was dominated by documentation maintenance, but several changes carry near-term operational consequences. Microsoft Defender XDR will treat Purview DLP alerts as behaviors by default from October 12; Defender for Endpoint support for Amazon Linux 2 ARM64 ends October 31; and Teams user reporting becomes enabled by default in late October, with an October 25 opt-out deadline. Defender for Endpoint on Linux also now requires tenant-specific service URLs in allowlists, while updated Linux guidance specifies enforcement modes and the prerequisite for audit mode.
2026-09.adminImpact: Decide whether to disable the new DLP behavior rule if DLP alerts must remain in the Defender XDR incident queue. Inventory Amazon Linux 2 ARM64 devices, prevent upgrades beyond version 101.25122.0004, and migrate them before October 31. Review Teams user-reporting settings and opt out by October 25 if needed. Add the required tenant-specific Defender for Endpoint Linux service URLs to allowlists. Before using Linux audit mode, verify version 101.26062.0007 or later and check the active antivirus_enforcement_level.

keyChanges.title: Amazon Linux 2 ARM64 support retires October 31
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint will stop providing updates and support for Amazon Linux 2 ARM64 after October 31, 2026. Administrators are directed to identify affected devices, prevent upgrades beyond version 101.25122.0004, and migrate to a supported Linux distribution.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP alerts become behaviors by default October 12
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender XDR will classify Microsoft Purview DLP alerts as behaviors by default, reducing alert volume while keeping DLP data available in Advanced Hunting and Purview. Administrators can disable the rule to retain DLP alerts in the Defender XDR incident queue.

keyChanges.title: Teams user reporting becomes the default for licensed organizations
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will enable Teams user reporting by default starting in late October 2026. Administrators can review the setting or opt out through a dedicated Defender portal page before October 25.

keyChanges.title: Linux endpoints need new tenant-specific Defender service URLs
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on Linux now requires allowlisting new service URLs specific to tenant types so devices can receive internal configuration updates, feature rollouts, and critical issue mitigations. The change is worldwide and does not change the user experience.

keyChanges.title: Linux antivirus guidance adds enforcement levels and an audit prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The Defender for Endpoint on Linux guidance now documents four antivirus enforcement levels, with passive as the default and audit mode marked Preview. Audit mode requires Defender for Endpoint version 101.26062.0007 or later, and the documented check uses the antivirus_enforcement_level value.

2026-10.headline: Advanced Hunting API retirement sets January migration deadline as Teams telemetry expands
2026-10.overview: October's clearest operational deadline is the retirement of the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs on February 1, 2027, with manual migration to the Microsoft Graph Security API required by January 31. In parallel, Defender for Office 365 is adding Teams message and call-and-meeting telemetry to Advanced Hunting, while Defender for Cloud guidance defines Azure commercial scope, configuration-loss implications, and Defender Workload Unit billing for portal-managed plans. A separate November RBAC change removes default Security Operator access to key email controls when Unified RBAC is enabled. Much of the remaining update volume was reference and procedural maintenance, concentrating the actionable work in these deadline, telemetry, portal-scope, and permissions changes.
2026-10.adminImpact: Inventory Advanced Hunting API consumers and complete the manual Microsoft Graph Security API migration by January 31, 2027. For Teams investigations, verify the permissions required for MessageContents and the Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 prerequisite for CallActivityEvents. Before moving Defender for Cloud plan management to the Defender portal, confirm Azure commercial eligibility and account for resource-level settings not being preserved, Azure portal settings becoming view-only, and DWU billing. Before the November RBAC change, review Unified RBAC assignments for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role and explicitly grant any required email-policy or Tenant Allow/Block List access.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting APIs retire with a January 31 migration deadline
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is retiring the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs on February 1, 2027. Organizations must manually migrate affected workflows to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027, to maintain functionality.

keyChanges.title: MessageContents brings Teams message data into Advanced Hunting
keyChanges.detail: Defender for Office 365 introduces the MessageContents table for querying Teams message snippets and metadata during threat investigations. Rollout runs from late September through mid-November 2026, and access requires specific permissions for authorized security analysts.

keyChanges.title: CallActivityEvents extends hunting to Teams calls and meetings
keyChanges.detail: Defender XDR adds the CallActivityEvents table for organizations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, covering activities, initiators, organizers, and related messages. The capability becomes available worldwide from November 2026 and integrates with Advanced Hunting, the event streaming API, and Microsoft Sentinel.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Cloud portal guidance defines migration scope and billing
keyChanges.detail: Updated integration guidance states that onboarding and plan management in the Defender portal currently support Azure commercial environments only, while cloud security data supports Azure, AWS, and GCP. After migration, plan settings become view-only in the Azure portal, resource-level configurations are not preserved, and billing uses Defender Workload Units.

keyChanges.title: Unified RBAC removes default Security Operator access to email controls
keyChanges.detail: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft Defender for Office 365's Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role removes default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List. Administrators must manually assign the permissions when Unified RBAC is enabled and continued access is needed.

2026-11.headline: Unified Defender RBAC activation and classic identity-alert retirements reshape security administration
2026-11.overview: November’s most consequential changes centered on access control, alert lifecycle, and response behavior. Unified Defender RBAC will auto-enable in December 2026, while the Microsoft Entra Security Operator mapping loses default access to key Defender for Office 365 controls. Two classic Defender for Identity alerts retire by late November, and Defender for Office 365 recipient matching will change from AND to OR when affected policies are modified. Plan 2 also adds a Move to Quarantine remediation action. Much of the Learn activity otherwise clarified prerequisites and scope, including local AI-agent discovery, Sentinel automation guidance, and a new page for controlling selected Defender for Endpoint preview features.
2026-11.adminImpact: Inventory and review imported Defender RBAC roles before activation, and explicitly assign Microsoft Entra Security Operator permissions where continued access to email threat policies or the Tenant Allow/Block List is required. Replace coverage for the retiring identity alerts, inspect threat-protection policies before modifying them because recipient scope can broaden, and migrate Sentinel playbooks that are invoked directly by analytics rules to automation rules. Plan 2’s Move to Quarantine rollout requires no mandatory action, but policy and role reviews are recommended. Administrators testing selected Endpoint previews must first enable the existing Preview features setting.

keyChanges.title: Unified Defender RBAC will auto-enable across Defender and Sentinel in December
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, Defender RBAC will be enabled automatically in the tenant, unifying access management for Defender and Sentinel. Existing roles are imported for review, with activation occurring about 30 days after notification; administrators can adjust roles as needed, and opt-out is available after activation. Permissions for other Microsoft services remain unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Entra Security Operator loses default access to key Defender for Office 365 controls
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in December 2026, the Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role removes default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List. Administrators must manually assign the required permissions if that access should continue.

keyChanges.title: Two classic Defender for Identity alerts retire by late November
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Identity will retire the “Remote code execution attempt” and “pass-the-hash” classic alerts by late November 2026. Microsoft directs administrators to create custom detection rules for RCE and rely on Defender for Endpoint for pass-the-hash monitoring.

keyChanges.title: Recipient matching changes from AND to OR when policies are modified
keyChanges.detail: In December 2026, Defender for Office 365 threat protection policies will use Match any (OR), rather than Match all (AND), when multiple recipient types are specified. Existing policies are not automatically converted, but modifying an affected policy can expand its scope.

keyChanges.title: Sentinel deprecates direct analytics-rule playbook invocation
keyChanges.detail: Alert-trigger playbooks and their Microsoft Sentinel Alert triggers remain supported, but direct invocation from analytics rules is deprecated. The updated procedure is to configure automation rules for alerts generated by one or multiple analytics rules.
